title: What the neural crest actually builds
lead: Neural crest builds the peripheral neurons and glia, melanocytes, the adrenal medulla, and the aorticopulmonary septum. It does not build the adrenal cortex.
lines: Facial cartilage and bone, odontoblasts, and thyroid C cells are crest.
The adrenal cortex is mesoderm. Thyroid follicular cells are endoderm.
A crest failure can connect a pigment problem, a heart outflow problem, and a missing adrenal medulla.
Crest derivatives include melanocytes, Schwann cells, dorsal-root ganglia, odontoblasts, and the adrenal medulla.
miss: Putting the adrenal cortex on the crest list because the medulla is there.

source.name: StatPearls. Neuroanatomy, Neural Crest.
source.says: Neural crest cells serve as precursors to a broad range of tissues, including melanocytes, sensory and autonomic ganglion neurons, and Schwann cells. Ectomesenchymal derivatives include neuroendocrine chromaffin cells of the adrenal medulla, dental mesenchymal stem (progenitor) cells and odontoblasts. Cardiac neural crest, a subset of cephalic neural crest extending from the otic level to the 4th somite, contributes to septation of the outflow tract.

title: DiGeorge is a pouch and a crest problem
lead: DiGeorge is the 22q11.2 deletion. It fails the third and fourth pharyngeal pouches and the neural crest that builds the outflow tract.
lines: No thymus and no parathyroids means infections and hypocalcemia. A neonatal seizure here is a low ionized calcium until the lab returns.
Third pouch: inferior parathyroids and thymus. Fourth pouch: superior parathyroids.
The heart lesion is conotruncal. Look at the outflow tract, not only the calcium.
The adrenal cortex is mesoderm and is not the missing gland.
miss: Treating the hypocalcemia and never looking at the heart or the immune system.

source.name: StatPearls. DiGeorge Syndrome.
source.says: TBX1 haploinsufficiency disrupts this process, leading to conotruncal malformations including tetralogy of Fallot, truncus arteriosus, interrupted aortic arch. Thymic hypoplasia or aplasia results from failed development of the thymic anlage from the third pharyngeal pouch. Parathyroid hypoplasia results from abnormal development of the parathyroid glands, which originate from the third and fourth pharyngeal pouches.

title: Turner is 45,X until proved otherwise
lead: Short stature, a webbed neck, coarctation, and streak ovaries in a girl is Turner syndrome until the karyotype says otherwise.
lines: The kidneys are often horseshoe or otherwise malformed. Check them.
Streak gonads do not produce a normal puberty.
Cystic hygroma and lymphedema in a newborn girl are the same diagnosis earlier.
miss: Calling it constitutional short stature because the blood pressure in the arms was never compared with the legs.

source.name: StatPearls. Turner Syndrome.
source.says: Disruption of X-chromosome material impairs normal growth and gonadal development, leading to characteristic features such as short stature, delayed puberty, primary amenorrhea, and neonatal lymphedema, as well as physical findings including a webbed neck and low-set ears. Common anomalies include a bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation of the aorta, an elongated transverse aortic arch, and pulmonary venous abnormalities.

more.name: Clinical practice guidelines for the care of girls and women with Turner syndrome (2024).

title: The four hypersensitivity types
lead: Type I is IgE and minutes. Type II is antibody on a cell. Type III is an immune complex. Type IV is T cells and delayed.
lines: Type I: anaphylaxis, asthma, nasal allergy. The mast cell was already coated.
Type II: autoimmune hemolysis, Goodpasture, acute rheumatic fever. Type III: serum sickness, Arthus reaction, lupus nephritis, post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.
Type IV: contact dermatitis, the tuberculosis skin test, and many drug rashes that appear days later.
miss: Calling a rash at day ten an allergy that should have happened in the first hour.
diagramAlt: Four types. I, IgE, minutes. II, antibody on a cell surface. III, immune complexes. IV, T cells, delayed.

source.name: StatPearls. Type I, Type II, Type III, and Type IV Hypersensitivity Reaction.
source.says: Type I hypersensitivity, also known as immediate hypersensitivity, is an immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated immune response. Type II hypersensitivity is an antibody-mediated reaction against cells or tissues of the body in which IgG or IgM antibodies bind to antigens on the surface of cells or tissues. Type III or immune complex-mediated hypersensitivity : Circulating antigen-antibody complexes deposit in tissues. Type IV hypersensitivity is a T-cell–mediated reaction with a delayed onset, typically appearing 48 to 72 hours after exposure to an allergen.

more.name: StatPearls. Type II Hypersensitivity Reaction.
StatPearls. Type III Hypersensitivity Reaction.
StatPearls. Type IV Hypersensitivity Reaction.

title: Which coagulation test moves
lead: PT tests factor VII and the common pathway. PTT tests factors XII, XI, IX, and VIII and the common pathway.
lines: The common pathway is X, V, II, and I. A defect there prolongs both tests.
Vitamin K factors are II, VII, IX, and X, plus proteins C and S. Warfarin drops them. Heparin potentiates antithrombin.
A mixing study corrects a missing factor. It does not correct an inhibitor.
miss: Expecting hemophilia to prolong the PT, or expecting warfarin to prolong only the PTT.

source.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Coagulation Pathways.
source.says: The extrinsic pathway is clinically assessed using the prothrombin time (PT). The intrinsic pathway is clinically assessed using the partial thromboplastin time (PTT). Mixing studies are performed to determine whether a PT or PTT is elevated due to a factor deficiency or a factor inhibitor (antibodies to specific factors).

title: Where complement starts, and where it meets
lead: Classical complement needs antibody. Alternative and lectin pathways do not. All three meet at C3.
lines: The complement proteins are made as inactive zymogens and need a cell surface to stay active.
Every pathway converts C3 to C3a and C3b. C3b is required for the membrane attack complex.
The proteins run from C1 to C9. The membrane attack complex lyses the cell.
miss: Teaching all three pathways as antibody-dependent, when only the classical pathway needs antibody.

source.name: StatPearls. Biochemistry, Complement.
source.says: One method of complement cascade initiation, the classical activation pathway, involves antibodies and, thus, the adaptive immune system. The alternative pathway can begin with the spontaneous conversion of C3 to C3b, microbial surface molecules, complex carbohydrates, or other substances. The lectin pathway utilizes complement proteins 2 and 4 to achieve the same result as the alternative pathway.

title: Sickle hemoglobin polymerizes when oxygen falls
lead: Hemoglobin S polymerizes when it is deoxygenated. That is the vaso-occlusive event, not an immune hemolysis.
lines: Howell-Jolly bodies mean the spleen is not clearing nuclear remnants. The patient is functionally asplenic.
Acute chest syndrome is a new infiltrate with chest pain, fever, or hypoxia. It is not a routine pneumonia to send home.
Hydroxyurea raises hemoglobin F and cuts the crises. It is not an acute pain drug.
miss: Giving iron for the anemia of sickle cell disease. The iron is not the missing piece.

source.name: StatPearls. Sickle Cell Disease.
source.says: Under conditions of reduced oxygen tension, deoxygenated HbS polymerizes, causing erythrocyte deformation, increased rigidity, hemolysis, and vaso-occlusion. HbS polymerization remains the initiating molecular event.

title: Spherocytes are a membrane problem
lead: Hereditary spherocytosis is a red-cell membrane defect. The cells are sphere-shaped, the MCHC is high, and the spleen removes them.
lines: Aplastic crisis after parvovirus drops the reticulocyte count. The hemolysis was already there.
Splenectomy is for severe disease, and it comes with a lifelong infection risk.
MCHC is high because membrane is lost. Osmotic fragility is increased. The spleen removes the spheres.
miss: Calling every spherocyte autoimmune hemolysis and starting steroids.
diagramAlt: Two hemolytic smears. Spherocytes, high MCHC: membrane Bite cells after an oxidant: G6PD G6PD level can be normal on the day

source.name: StatPearls. Hereditary Spherocytosis.
source.says: Hereditary spherocytosis (HS) is the most prevalent cause of hemolytic anemia due to an abnormal red cell membrane. Membrane loss results in spherocytosis, a drop in mean corpuscular volume (MCV), an increase in mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC), and increased osmotic fragility of RBCs. Spherocytes are destroyed and cleared from circulation during passage through the spleen.

title: Do not trust a G6PD level on the day of the hemolysis
lead: G6PD deficiency is X-linked. Oxidant stress hemolyzes the oldest red cells, and an enzyme level drawn that day can look normal.
lines: Sulfa drugs, primaquine, dapsone, infection, and fava beans are the usual triggers.
Repeat the assay weeks later, after the depleted cells have been replaced.
Heinz bodies are denatured hemoglobin. Bite cells are the smear after the spleen bites them out.
miss: Ruling out the deficiency because the assay during the crisis was normal.

source.name: StatPearls. Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase Deficiency.
source.says: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency is an X-linked enzymatic disorder affecting cellular defense against oxidative stress. After resolution of an acute episode, clinicians should repeat a quantitative G6PD assay to confirm enzyme deficiency, as testing during hemolysis can yield false-normal results.

title: Methylmalonic acid separates B12 from folate
lead: Both B12 and folate deficiency make a megaloblastic anemia. Only B12 raises methylmalonic acid and injures the cord.
lines: Homocysteine is high in both. It does not separate them.
Folate alone can fix the anemia of B12 deficiency and leave the neurologic injury going.
Vegans, pernicious anemia, and terminal ileum disease are the usual B12 stories. Folate deficiency is diet, alcohol, and pregnancy.
Folate can fix the anemia and leave subacute combined degeneration going. Never treat a high MCV with folate alone.
miss: Treating a high mean corpuscular volume with folate before the B12 status is known.
diagramAlt: B12 versus folate. Both: high MCV, high homocysteine Only B12: high methylmalonic acid Folate alone can hide the cord injury

source.name: StatPearls. Vitamin B12 Deficiency.
source.says: In patients with B12 deficiency, methylmalonic acid (MMA) levels will accumulate, as it cannot be converted to succinyl-CoA. These lab values can also help to distinguish B12 deficiency from folate deficiency, in which homocysteine levels are elevated but MMA levels are normal. The damage to the myelin results in a condition known as subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord (SCDSC).

title: Hemophilia A is factor VIII, and the PT is normal
lead: Hemophilia A is factor VIII deficiency, X-linked, and it prolongs the PTT. The PT stays normal.
lines: The bleeding is into joints and muscle, not tiny skin bleeds.
A mixing study corrects, because the factor is missing and there is no inhibitor yet.
Hemophilia B is factor IX. The clinical picture is the same and the assay is not.
PT is normal. PTT is long and corrects with mixing unless an inhibitor has formed.
miss: Expecting the PT to be prolonged, or calling a hemarthrosis von Willebrand disease without a factor level.

source.name: StatPearls. Hemophilia A.
source.says: Hemophilia A, the most common form, is caused by a deficiency or dysfunction of coagulation factor VIII and is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern. An isolated prolongation of activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) with normal prothrombin time (PT) and platelet count is the most common laboratory finding.

title: Von Willebrand disease is a platelet-function disease that can prolong the PTT
lead: Von Willebrand disease is the common inherited bleeding disorder. The bleeding is mucosal, and the PTT is prolonged only when factor VIII is low enough.
lines: Type 1 responds to desmopressin. Type 2B can get worse with it, because the abnormal multimer binds platelets.
Ristocetin cofactor activity is the functional test.
vWF carries factor VIII. Mucosal bleeding with a normal platelet count is the picture. PTT prolongs only if VIII is low.
miss: Giving desmopressin to every subtype, including type 2B.
diagramAlt: Desmopressin in VWD. Type 1: desmopressin often works Type 2B: desmopressin can drop platelets Mucosal bleeding. PTT may be normal

source.name: StatPearls. Von Willebrand Disease.
source.says: Affected people may complain of excessive bruising, prolonged bleeding from mucosal surfaces, and prolonged bleeding after minor trauma. Von Willebrand factor increases factor VIII half-life by preventing its degradation. Coagulation profile: aPTT may be prolonged, as there would be increased factor VIII degradation in von Willebrand disease.

more.name: ASH ISTH NHF WFH 2021 guidelines on the management of von Willebrand disease.

title: DIC is a consumption, and the fibrinogen falls
lead: Disseminated intravascular coagulation consumes platelets and clotting factors. Fibrinogen is low, D-dimer is high, and both the PT and the PTT prolong.
lines: The treatment is the cause: sepsis, trauma, obstetric catastrophe, or acute promyelocytic leukemia.
Cryoprecipitate replaces fibrinogen. Platelets are for bleeding, not for a number alone.
A chronic cancer DIC can be compensated and look quieter. Do not wait for every lab to be abnormal before treating the cause.
Fibrinogen falls, D-dimer rises, PT and PTT prolong, and platelets fall.
miss: Treating the labs with heparin as the first move in a bleeding patient.
diagramAlt: DIC labs. Low fibrinogen, high D-dimer PT and PTT both prolong Cryoprecipitate if bleeding and fibrinogen is low

source.name: StatPearls. Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation.
source.says: As this process begins consuming clotting factors and platelets in a positive feedback loop, hemorrhage can ensue. Laboratory findings suggestive of DIC include an increased prothrombin time (PT) and an increased partial thromboplastin time, as well as a decreased fibrinogen level as widespread activation and consumption of the clotting cascade occurs. This score includes platelet count, fibrin markers such as D-dimer, PT, and fibrinogen level.

title: ITP is isolated thrombocytopenia
lead: Immune thrombocytopenia drops the platelet count and leaves the red cells and white cells alone. There are no schistocytes.
lines: Children often follow a virus and recover. Adults are more often chronic.
Bleeding, not the number, drives treatment in a stable patient. Steroids or IVIG are the usual first drugs when treatment is needed.
TTP is the one with microangiopathic hemolysis. Do not mix them.
No schistocytes and the other cell lines are normal. That is the split from TTP.
Treat bleeding or a planned procedure. A platelet transfusion does not last and is reserved for serious bleeding.
miss: Transfusing platelets as the treatment of ITP in a patient who is not bleeding.
diagramAlt: TTP versus ITP. TTP: schistocytes, hemolysis, exchange now ITP: isolated low platelets, no fragments Platelets in TTP only for life-threatening bleed

source.name: StatPearls. Immune Thrombocytopenia.
source.says: Primary ITP manifests with isolated thrombocytopenia. Schistocytosis usually signifies microangiopathic hemolytic anemia.

title: ALL is a disease of lymphoblasts
lead: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia is an accumulation of lymphoblasts. It is the acute leukemia of children, and the blasts are TdT positive.
lines: Lymphoblasts are TdT positive. Auer rods are myeloid and exclude ALL. Peak age is about 2–5 years.
T-lymphoblastic disease can present with a mediastinal mass and airway symptoms.
Bone pain and cytopenias in a child are ALL until the marrow is read. The other cell lines are often low.
miss: Calling every childhood blast crisis myeloid because the child looks sick.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia/Lymphoblastic Lymphoma.
source.says: ALL is primarily a disease of children younger than 6 years with a slight male predominance. Early precursor B-ALL, or pro-B-ALL, expresses CD19, cytoplasmic C079a, cytoplasmic CD22, and nuclear TdT.

title: Myeloma is CRAB, not a high white count
lead: Multiple myeloma is a plasma-cell cancer. The clinical set is calcium high, renal failure, anemia, and bone lesions.
lines: Rouleaux are red cells stacked by paraprotein. The white count is not the story.
Lytic bone lesions do not light up on a bone scan the way blastic prostate lesions do.
CRAB is calcium, renal failure, anemia, and lytic bone. Light chains can be missed by a urine dipstick for albumin.
miss: Ordering a technetium bone scan to find the lytic lesions, or reassuring a normal albumin dipstick.

source.name: StatPearls. Multiple Myeloma.
source.says: Multiple myeloma is a clonal plasma cell proliferative disorder characterized by the abnormal increase of monoclonal immunoglobulins. CRAB (hypercalcemia, renal dysfunction, anemia, and/or bone pain with lytic lesions).

title: Tumor lysis drops calcium and raises everything else
lead: Tumor lysis releases cell contents. Potassium, phosphate, and uric acid rise. Calcium falls because it binds the phosphate.
lines: The risk is highest as treatment starts in a bulky, fast cancer.
Fluids come first. Rasburicase is for a high uric acid or a high-risk patient. Allopurinol does not clear uric acid that is already there.
The arrhythmia is the potassium. Treat that before the uric acid chart.
Established tumor lysis with a high uric acid is treated with rasburicase, after fluids, and calcium falls as phosphate rises.
miss: Giving calcium for the low number without looking at the potassium and the phosphate.
diagramAlt: Tumor lysis ions. K up, phosphate up, uric acid up Calcium down (binds phosphate) Rasburicase clears uric acid already made

source.name: StatPearls. Tumor Lysis Syndrome.
source.says: Tumor lysis syndrome is a clinical condition caused by extensive tumor cell lysis and characterized by metabolic disturbances, such as hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, and hyperuricemia, which can lead to end-organ damage. Calcium-phosphorus salt deposits can form in the kidneys and soft tissues. The primary prophylactic strategies are IV hydration and hypouricemic agents such as allopurinol and rasburicase.

more.name: BSH guideline for the management of tumour lysis syndrome (2015).

title: A hemolytic transfusion reaction means stop the blood
lead: Fever, back pain, and dark urine during a transfusion is acute hemolysis until proved otherwise. Stop the unit.
lines: Clerical error and ABO incompatibility are the classic cause.
Do not restart that unit because the fever might be cytokines. Prove it first.
ABO mismatch causes fever, flank pain, and hemoglobinuria during the transfusion. Stop that unit.
Keep the bag. Send it back with a fresh sample. Clerical error is the usual cause. Do not restart the same unit.
miss: Slowing the rate and giving acetaminophen while the urine turns red.

source.name: StatPearls. Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction.
source.says: Classically, an acute HTR is described as a triad of symptoms: fever, flank pain, and red or brown urine (hemoglobinuria). The first step is always to stop the transfusion.

title: PNH is complement on red cells that lost their shield
lead: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria is acquired loss of CD55 and CD59. Complement punches the red cells, and the urine is dark in the morning.
lines: Thrombosis in an unusual vein, including the hepatic vein, is the dangerous part.
The test is flow cytometry for the missing GPI-anchored proteins, not a smear.
A complement inhibitor such as eculizumab or a newer C5 or proximal inhibitor is the disease-modifying treatment.
miss: Calling dark morning urine myoglobinuria and ordering a CK only.

source.name: StatPearls. Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria.
source.says: Proteins responsible for the regulation of complement activity, specifically CD55 and CD59, are thereby prevented from attaching to PNH affected cells. It causes complications mainly through intravascular hemolysis, thrombosis, and bone marrow failure. This mutation of the X-linked gene phosphatidylinositol glycan class A (PIGA), produces a deficiency in the glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) protein.

more.name: ACIP recommendations for meningococcal vaccination (complement inhibitor users).

title: Aplastic anemia is an empty marrow
lead: Aplastic anemia is pancytopenia with a low reticulocyte count and a marrow that is empty. The spleen is not big.
lines: A big spleen and an abnormal smear point at a production problem of a different kind, or at sequestration.
Drugs, benzene, viruses, and immune attack are the usual stories.
Transfusion is support. It is not the diagnosis, and it can sensitize a patient who may need a transplant.
Reticulocytes are low and the marrow is empty. Splenomegaly argues against aplastic anemia.
Avoid family-directed donor blood if transplant is possible. Those transfusions can sensitize the recipient.
miss: Diagnosing leukemia because all three lines are low, without a marrow.

source.name: StatPearls. Aplastic Anemia.
source.says: Aplastic anemia is a rare but serious hematologic disorder characterized by the failure of bone marrow to produce enough blood cells, leading to pancytopenia. Hypocellular marrow with fatty replacement. Absence of liver, spleen, and lymph node enlarg.

title: Polycythemia vera suppresses EPO
lead: Polycythemia vera is a JAK2-driven red-cell mass. Erythropoietin is low, because the marrow is not being asked.
lines: Aquagenic pruritus, erythromelalgia, and a high hematocrit are the clues.
A high EPO means the body is responding to hypoxia or a tumor. That is not this disease.
Phlebotomy lowers the hematocrit. It does not treat secondary polycythemia from lung disease.
A high EPO is secondary erythrocytosis.
Do not apply that target to hypoxic lung disease.
miss: Giving oxygen or a workup for hypoxia as the only plan when the EPO is already low.
diagramAlt: Polycythemia vera target. JAK2. EPO is low Phlebotomy toward hematocrit <45% Do not phlebotomize hypoxic high-EPO disease

source.name: StatPearls. Polycythemia Vera.
source.says: The Janus kinase-2 (JAK2) gene involved with intracellular signaling is mutated in 90% of cases of polycythemia vera (PV). Serum erythropoietin level below the reference range for normal.

title: Auer rods mean myeloid, and APL is the DIC emergency
lead: Auer rods are fused granules in myeloid blasts. Acute promyelocytic leukemia, among the myeloid leukemias, consumes clotting factors and is treated with all-trans retinoic acid.
lines: Do not wait for the karyotype to start ATRA when the smear and the coagulopathy say promyelocytic leukemia.
The translocation is t(15;17). The drug targets that differentiation block.
Bleeding, not infection, is the early death in this subtype.
Fibrinogen falls, D-dimer rises, PT and PTT prolong, and platelets fall.
Cryoprecipitate is the product that replaces fibrinogen. Platelets are for bleeding, not for a daily threshold.
miss: Treating every AML the same and discovering the coagulopathy after a procedure.
diagramAlt: DIC labs. Low fibrinogen, high D-dimer PT and PTT both prolong Cryoprecipitate if bleeding and fibrinogen is low

source.name: ELN expert-panel recommendations for the management of acute promyelocytic leukemia.
source.says: ATRA should be initiated immediately once APL is suspected. Transfusions of fibrinogen and/or cryoprecipitate, platelets, and fresh-frozen plasma should be given to maintain the fibrinogen concentration above 100 to 150 mg/dL and the platelet count above 30 to 50 × 10^9/L.

title: Reed-Sternberg cells are Hodgkin, not the non-Hodgkin list
lead: A Reed-Sternberg cell defines classic Hodgkin lymphoma. Non-Hodgkin lymphomas are a different group of lymphocyte cancers and do not use that cell as the diagnosis.
lines: Hodgkin disease often spreads to contiguous nodes and is treated with a regimen built for it.
B symptoms are fever, night sweats, and weight loss. They change the stage conversation, not the cell type.
A single node name does not pick the regimen.
miss: Calling every lymphoma Hodgkin because a node is present.

source.name: StatPearls. Hodgkin Lymphoma.
source.says: They commonly arise in the cervical lymph nodes; the disease is more common in young adults; there are scattered large mononuclear Hodgkin and multinucleated cells (Reed-Sternberg) intermixed in a background of a mixture of non-neoplastic inflammatory cells; finally, T lymphocytes are often observed surrounding the characteristic neoplastic cells.

title: The receptor, the G protein, the effect
lead: Alpha-1 and M3 are Gq. Alpha-2 and M2 are Gi. Beta-1 and beta-2 are Gs, and beta-1 speeds the heart.
lines: Alpha-1 constricts vessels, dilates the pupil, and contracts the bladder sphincter.
Beta-1 raises heart rate, contractility, and renin. Beta-2 opens bronchi, dilates skeletal muscle vessels, and relaxes the uterus.
M2 slows the heart. M3 increases secretions, constricts bronchi, contracts the detrusor, and constricts the pupil.
miss: Giving a beta blocker for wheeze, or expecting alpha-1 block to slow the heart rate.

source.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Muscarinic Receptor; Alpha-Adrenergic Receptors; Beta 1 Receptors.
source.says: M1, M3, M5 are stimulatory receptors and are composed of the Gq protein, whereas M2 and M4 receptors are inhibitory receptors and are composed of the Gi protein. The alpha-1 receptor is of the Gq type, resulting in activation of phospholipase C. The alpha-2 receptor acts as an allosteric inhibitor through Gi function. The beta-1 adrenergic receptor is a G-protein-coupled receptor communicating through the Gs alpha subunit.

more.name: StatPearls. Beta 1 Receptors.

title: One cut through half the cord
lead: Brown-Séquard loses motor and proprioception on the same side, and pain and temperature a level or two below on the other side.
lines: The corticospinal tract has already crossed in the medulla, so the weakness is ipsilateral.
Dorsal columns have not crossed yet, so vibration and position sense are ipsilateral.
Spinothalamic fibers cross within a segment or two, so pain and temperature loss is contralateral and slightly below the cut.
A cut at one level weakens the ipsilateral arm and leg and removes ipsilateral vibration at that level.
Pain and temperature are lost on the opposite side, beginning one or two segments below the cut, because those fibers cross in the cord.
miss: Putting all three losses on the same side.

source.name: StatPearls. Brown-Séquard Syndrome.
source.says: Manifestations of this neurologic syndrome include weakness or paralysis, proprioceptive deficits on the side of the body ipsilateral to the lesion, and loss of pain and temperature sensation on the contralateral side.

title: Which artery, which deficit
lead: Middle cerebral artery is the face and the arm. Anterior cerebral artery is the leg. Posterior cerebral artery is the visual cortex.
lines: A dominant middle cerebral lesion also takes language. A nondominant lesion takes attention to the other side.
Anterior cerebral infarction spares the arm relative to the leg and can mute the patient.
Posterior cerebral infarction causes a contralateral visual-field cut. Motor strength can be intact.
MCA is face and arm. ACA is leg. PCA is a visual-field cut that can spare strength.
miss: Calling a dense arm-and-face deficit an anterior cerebral stroke because the patient cannot walk.

source.name: StatPearls. Middle Cerebral Artery Stroke; Anterior Cerebral Artery Stroke; Posterior Cerebral Artery Stroke.
source.says: The MCA, a key branch of the internal carotid artery, supplies extensive cortical and subcortical regions, so occlusions are highly symptomatic, with deficits such as hemiparesis, aphasia, neglect, and visual field loss. Most commonly, patients present with motor deficits, typically involving the lower extremity contralateral to the infarct site. Unilateral occipital lobe infarction commonly produces contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing.

more.name: StatPearls. Anterior Cerebral Artery Stroke.
StatPearls. Posterior Cerebral Artery Stroke.

title: Epidural blood is a lens and a lucid interval
lead: An epidural hematoma is arterial, usually the middle meningeal artery, lens-shaped, and it does not cross suture lines.
lines: The classic course is a hit, a lucid interval, then a collapse.
The bleed is under arterial pressure, so the decline is fast.
A lens on CT in a patient who is talking and then not is this, not a migraine.
Middle meningeal artery, lens shape, does not cross sutures. Lucid interval then collapse.
A dilating pupil is uncal herniation. That patient goes to the operating room. Do not wait for the next scheduled scan.
miss: Sending the lucid patient home because the first exam was normal.

source.name: StatPearls. Epidural Hematoma.
source.says: Most EDHs result from arterial bleeding, typically from a branch of the middle meningeal artery. The hematoma’s expansion is often restricted by cranial sutures, producing a characteristic biconvex shape on noncontrast head computed tomography.

title: Subdural blood is a crescent from bridging veins
lead: A subdural hematoma is venous blood from bridging veins. It is crescent-shaped and it can cross suture lines.
lines: Bridging veins tear in an atrophied brain. The crescent can cross sutures and declare itself days later.
Anticoagulation turns a small tear into a large collection.
Reverse the anticoagulant for any anticoagulant-associated subdural hematoma. Size does not keep the drug going.
A lens that stops at sutures is epidural arterial blood, not this venous crescent.
miss: Leaving the anticoagulant on because the subdural hematoma looks small or the symptoms came on slowly.

source.name: StatPearls. Subdural Hematoma.
source.says: Rupture of thin-walled bridging veins under opposing mechanical forces releases blood into the subdural space, resulting in a subdural hematoma. The classic appearance involves a crescent-shaped collection that crosses suture lines while remaining limited by the falx and tentorium.

more.name: NCS/SCCM guideline for reversal of antithrombotics in intracranial hemorrhage (2016).

title: A deep bleed and a lobar bleed are different diseases
lead: A hypertensive bleed prefers the deep structures: putamen, thalamus, pons, cerebellum. A lobar bleed in an older adult is amyloid until proved otherwise.
lines: The cerebellum is the one that herniates and obstructs. It is a surgical conversation.
Blood pressure is part of the cause in the deep bleed and part of the treatment in both.
Do not call every brain bleed a ruptured aneurysm. Aneurysms live in the subarachnoid space.
miss: Waiting for an angiogram before treating a cerebellar hemorrhage that is already compressing the brainstem.
diagramAlt: Which bleed goes to surgery. Cerebellum with compression: evacuate Putamen: usually medical Lobar in an older adult: think amyloid

source.name: StatPearls. Hemorrhagic Stroke Overview.
source.says: Common sites of bleeding include the basal ganglia (40%-50%), the thalamus (20%-25%), the cerebral lobes (15%-20%), the cerebellum (10%-15%), and the pons and brainstem (5%-10%). Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) is a leading cause of primary lobar intracerebral hemorrhage in older adults.

title: Parkinson disease is a substantia nigra problem
lead: Parkinson disease loses dopamine cells in the substantia nigra. The motor set is rest tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, and a posture that fails.
lines: The tremor is at rest and improves with action. A cerebellar tremor does the opposite.
Lewy bodies are the inclusion. They are not required on a scan to start treatment.
A drug that blocks dopamine can copy the picture. Stop the drug before diagnosing the disease.
Rest tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia from nigral dopamine loss. Give hospital doses at the home clock times.
Metoclopramide and haloperidol block dopamine and copy the disease. Levodopa is the most effective motor drug.
miss: Calling an action tremor Parkinson disease and starting levodopa.
diagramAlt: Parkinson doses in hospital. Give carbidopa-levodopa at home times No metoclopramide or haloperidol Levodopa is the strongest motor drug

source.name: StatPearls. Parkinson Disease.
source.says: The degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, accompanied by the intracellular accumulation of alpha-synuclein (α-synuclein) (Lewy body), represents the neuropathological hallmark of the disease. Clinical presentation most commonly begins with asymmetric motor features, including bradykinesia, resting tremor, rigidity, and postural instability.

title: Multiple sclerosis is separated in time and in space
lead: Multiple sclerosis is neurologic lesions separated in time and in space. Oligoclonal bands in the spinal fluid support it.
lines: Optic neuritis, internuclear ophthalmoplegia, and a sensory level are the usual episodes.
Symptoms that worsen with heat are a clue, not a diagnosis.
Dissemination in time and space, plus unmatched oligoclonal bands. One lesion is not the disease.
A new disabling deficit can get high-dose steroids. The same old deficit plus a fever is infection until proved otherwise.
miss: Diagnosing multiple sclerosis from one MRI spot and a week of fatigue.
diagramAlt: MS flare versus infection. New deficit: high-dose steroid Old deficit plus fever: find the infection Disease-modifying drug is a separate order

source.name: StatPearls. Multiple Sclerosis.
source.says: Although various diagnostic criteria exist for multiple sclerosis, the general principle for diagnosing the relapsing-remitting course involves establishing episodes separated in "time and space." The classic abnormal CSF findings in multiple sclerosis typically include elevated protein and myelin basic protein levels, occasional leukocytes (mainly mononuclear cells), and increased levels of total immunoglobulin G (IgG), free kappa light chains, and oligoclonal bands.

title: Guillain-Barré climbs, and the spinal fluid protein climbs later
lead: Guillain-Barré syndrome is an ascending paralysis with lost reflexes after an infection, often Campylobacter.
lines: IVIg 0.4 g/kg daily for 5 days if the patient cannot walk unaided and weakness began within 2 weeks. A good-practice point also allows 2 to 4 weeks.
Or plasma exchange, 12–15 L in four to five exchanges over 1 to 2 weeks, if weakness began within 4 weeks and the patient cannot walk unaided.
Do not use oral corticosteroids. A second course of IVIg for a poor prognosis is recommended against.
Use the modified Erasmus GBS Respiratory Insufficiency Score for the ventilation risk. CSF examination is valuable when the diagnosis is uncertain.
miss: Starting prednisone, or quoting a vital-capacity cutoff this guideline does not use, instead of IVIg or plasma exchange.
diagramAlt: Guillain-Barré breathing. IVIG or exchange. Not prednisone Vital capacity under 20 mL/kg: intubate window CSF: high protein, almost no cells

source.name: EAN/PNS guideline on diagnosis and treatment of Guillain-Barré syndrome.
source.says: The task force recommends IVIg 0.4 g/kg for 5 days within 2 weeks (GPP also within 2-4 weeks) after onset of weakness if unable to walk unaided, or plasma exchange 12-15 L in four to five exchanges over 1-2 weeks within 4 weeks; it recommends against oral corticosteroids and advises the mEGRIS score for ventilation risk.

title: Absence seizures are 3-hertz and have no postictal state
lead: A childhood absence seizure is a few seconds of staring, a 3-hertz spike and wave, and an immediate return. There is no postictal confusion.
lines: Ethosuximide is the drug for absence alone.
Hyperventilation in the office can provoke it.
A generalized tonic-clonic drug such as carbamazepine can worsen pure absence.
Carbamazepine can worsen absence. Hyperventilation in clinic can reproduce the spell.
Ethosuximide if this is the only seizure type.
miss: Treating staring spells with carbamazepine because all seizures look the same.
diagramAlt: Absence drug. 3 Hz spike-and-wave. No postictal state Ethosuximide if absence is the only seizure Carbamazepine can worsen pure absence

source.name: StatPearls. Absence Seizure.
source.says: Absence seizures are brief seizures characterized by a behavioral arrest correlating with generalized 3-Hz spike and wave discharges on electroencephalogram (EEG). These seizures are not preceded by an aura and do not have a postictal state.

title: Horner syndrome is a sympathetic cut
lead: Horner syndrome is ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis from a lost sympathetic path to the eye and the face.
lines: A lung apex tumor, a carotid dissection, and a brainstem stroke sit on that path.
The pupil is small, not blown. The lid droops a little, not over the pupil completely.
Anhidrosis localizes the lesion to before the superior cervical ganglion when it is present.
Ptosis and miosis from lost sympathetics. A third-nerve palsy is a down-and-out eye with a blown pupil.
miss: Calling a small pupil a third-nerve palsy. A third-nerve palsy blows the pupil and downs the eye.

source.name: StatPearls. Horner Syndrome.
source.says: Horner syndrome is a rare condition classically presenting with partial ptosis (drooping of the upper eyelid), miosis (pupillary constriction), and facial anhidrosis (loss of sweating) due to disruption of the sympathetic nerve supply.

title: Bell palsy includes the forehead
lead: A peripheral facial nerve lesion weakens the whole half of the face, forehead included. A cortical stroke spares the forehead.
lines: Bell palsy is the idiopathic peripheral lesion. The eye does not close, so the cornea dries.
Ear pain and vesicles mean zoster, not idiopathic palsy.
Steroids early help idiopathic Bell palsy. They are not the treatment of a stroke.
Forehead weakness means the lesion is peripheral. Forehead sparing is a central lesion and a stroke pathway.
miss: Sending a forehead-sparing facial droop home as Bell palsy.
diagramAlt: Bell palsy, first 72 hours. Forehead involved = peripheral nerve Prednisone early. Lubricate the eye Forehead spared = stroke pathway

source.name: StatPearls. Bell Palsy.
source.says: Upon physical examination, all branches of the facial nerve are roughly equally impaired on the affected side of the face in patients with Bell palsy. In contrast, a cortical stroke will typically leave forehead movement intact on the affected side due to bilateral upper motor neuron contributions to the facial nucleus.

title: Trigeminal neuralgia is a shock, and carbamazepine is the drug
lead: Trigeminal neuralgia is seconds of electric pain in one trigeminal branch, set off by touch, and carbamazepine is the first drug.
lines: A continuous face pain is not this disease.
A young patient or a sensory loss needs imaging for a compressive or demyelinating lesion.
The drug's own risks, including low sodium and a rash, are part of the prescription.
Seconds of pain in one division. Carbamazepine is first-line. Hyponatremia and rash are the drug harms.
miss: Treating electric facial pain with a dental extraction and no drug.
diagramAlt: Trigeminal neuralgia. Seconds of shock in one branch Carbamazepine first Check sodium. Young or numb: image

source.name: AAN/EFNS practice parameter. Diagnostic evaluation and treatment of trigeminal neuralgia.
source.says: Carbamazepine (Level A) or oxcarbazepine (Level B) should be offered for pain control in trigeminal neuralgia, while baclofen and lamotrigine (Level C) may be considered useful.

title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is rigid and slow
lead: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome follows a dopamine blocker. The body is rigid, the reflexes are not clonus, and the creatine kinase is high.
lines: Stop the drug. Cool the patient. Support the pressure.
A dopamine agonist or dantrolene is the specific conversation, not another antipsychotic.
Serotonin syndrome is the opposite motor picture: clonus and hyperreflexia.
Lead-pipe rigidity and high CK over days. Reflexes are reduced, not clonic.
Stop the dopamine blocker. Do not give another dose for agitation. Cooling and fluids for the muscle breakdown.
miss: Giving more of the antipsychotic because the patient is agitated.
diagramAlt: NMS versus serotonin syndrome. NMS: lead-pipe, high CK, days Serotonin: clonus, hours, two drugs Stop the offending drug in both

source.name: StatPearls. Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
source.says: The primary trigger for NMS is dopamine receptor blockade, most often due to an antipsychotic agent. Classic clinical characteristics include mental status changes, fever, muscle rigidity, and autonomic instability. Diagnosis can be made clinically, but supporting lab work is usually consistent with rhabdomyolysis with an elevated CK and acutely declining renal function.

title: Serotonin syndrome has clonus
lead: Serotonin syndrome is clonus, hyperreflexia, and fever after a serotonergic drug, often two of them together.
lines: The legs are jumpy, not lead-pipe.
Stop the drugs. A benzodiazepine treats the agitation. Cyproheptadine is the antidote conversation.
It can start in hours. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome takes days.
Clonus and hyperreflexia within hours of an SSRI plus an MAOI, linezolid, tramadol, or a triptan. Stop both drugs on that shift.
miss: Adding an MAOI or a triptan or linezolid to an SSRI and calling the shivering a virus.
diagramAlt: NMS versus serotonin syndrome. NMS: lead-pipe, high CK, days Serotonin: clonus, hours, two drugs Stop the offending drug in both

source.name: StatPearls. Serotonin Syndrome.
source.says: A classic feature of serotonin syndrome is neuromuscular hyperactivity, which typically presents as hyperreflexia and myoclonus. Physical exam findings may include altered mental status (with agitation), ocular clonus, dilated pupils, akathisia, tremor, deep tendon hyperreflexia, inducible (or spontaneous) muscle clonus.

title: Lithium has a narrow window and wastes water
lead: Lithium toxicity is tremor, confusion, and a level that does not have to be far above the range. Chronic use causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
lines: Thiazides, NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, and dehydration raise the level.
The kidney cannot concentrate urine, so the patient drinks and urinates.
Dialysis is for a severe level or a severe brain, not for a mild tremor alone.
miss: Starting a thiazide or an NSAID and never rechecking the level.
diagramAlt: Lithium interactions. NSAIDs, thiazides, ACE inhibitors raise it Hold the drug. Severe toxicity: dialysis Chronic use: nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

source.name: StatPearls. Lithium Toxicity.
source.says: Toxicity is a concern because lithium has a narrow therapeutic index, and renal excretion without hepatic metabolism is its only clinically meaningful elimination pathway. Examples include dehydration, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, and low-sodium diets.

title: Tardive dyskinesia outlasts the drug
lead: Tardive dyskinesia is repetitive mouth and trunk movements after months of a dopamine blocker, and stopping the drug may not stop the movements.
lines: It is not acute dystonia, which is hours after a dose and answers to an anticholinergic.
It is not akathisia, which is restlessness.
A VMAT2 inhibitor is the treatment conversation. Another first-generation antipsychotic is not.
Months of a blocker, then orofacial movements that can persist after the drug stops.
miss: Treating mouth movements with more of the drug that caused them, unless a specialist is treating withdrawal carefully.

source.name: StatPearls. Tardive Dyskinesia.
source.says: Tardive dyskinesia is a potentially irreversible hyperkinetic movement disorder resulting from prolonged exposure to dopamine receptor–block. The condition develops gradually, with symptoms emerging months or years after treatment initiation, and persists or worsens after discontinuation of the causative agent.

title: Alzheimer disease starts with memory, not a sudden deficit
lead: Alzheimer disease is a gradual loss of memory from hippocampal amyloid and tau. A sudden deficit is a stroke until proved otherwise.
lines: Cholinesterase inhibitors do not reverse the plaques. They may slow the symptoms a little.
Early personality change and disinhibition point at the frontal lobe, not this disease.
Normal pressure hydrocephalus is gait first, then bladder, then cognition, with large ventricles.
Gradual episodic memory. A deficit that starts today is a stroke or delirium until worked up.
Diphenhydramine and other anticholinergics worsen cognition. Cholinesterase inhibitors do not reverse plaques.
miss: Starting a dementia drug for a deficit that appeared this morning.

source.name: StatPearls. Alzheimer Disease.
source.says: The neurodegenerative process typically begins in the entorhinal cortex within the hippocampus. Neurofibrillary tangles first appear in the hippocampus and subsequently spread throughout the cerebral cortex. Neurofibrillary tangles are fibrillary intracytoplasmic structures that form inside neurons and are composed of a protein called tau.

title: Normal pressure hydrocephalus is gait, bladder, then mind
lead: Normal pressure hydrocephalus is a magnetic gait, urinary incontinence, and dementia, in that order of usefulness, with large ventricles and a pressure that is not high.
lines: The gait improves with a tap or a shunt in the patients who are going to respond.
A cortical dementia does not start with the feet.
The scan looks like atrophy until you notice the ventricles are out of proportion.
Gait, then bladder, then cognition. Ventricles large, cortex relatively spared, opening pressure not high.
A tap that improves gait is the patient considered for a shunt. Memory-first disease is not shunted.
miss: Diagnosing Alzheimer disease in a patient whose walking failed first.

source.name: StatPearls. Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus.
source.says: Typically, iNPH primarily affects older adults and characteristically presents with progressive gait impairment, cognitive deficits, and urinary urgency or incontinence, a constellation known as the Hakim–Adams triad, first described by Colombian neurosurgeon Salomon Hakim and R D Adams in 1965. Typical gait descriptors include shuffling, magnetic, and wide-based patterns, accompanied by increased mediolateral variability during quiet standing.

title: A brain abscess is a ring, and a lumbar puncture is the wrong next test
lead: A brain abscess is a ring-enhancing mass, often from a sinus, an ear, or a heart valve. Lumbar puncture is not the next test when a mass is present.
lines: The headache is progressive. Fever can be missing.
Streptococci and mixed mouth organisms are the contiguous story. Staph is the postoperative and trauma story.
Drain plus antibiotics, not antibiotics alone, when the collection is large.
Image before the lumbar puncture when a focal sign or papilledema is present.
miss: Performing a lumbar puncture for fever and headache before imaging a patient with a focal sign.

source.name: StatPearls. Brain Abscess.
source.says: Enzmann et al reported that CT findings of patchy enhancements in early cerebritis evolve into more distinct ring-like enhancements in late cerebritis, eventually forming a frank rim-enhancing brain abscess. Abscesses often arise from local infections in areas such as the ear, teeth, sinuses, mastoid air cells, or epidural spaces, but they may also originate from distant sites such as the lungs or heart. Rarely required, a lumbar puncture should only be performed after obtaining a head computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to rule out increased intracranial pressure due to significant mass effect, which can lead to cerebral herniation and potential mortality.

more.name: ESCMID guideline on diagnosis and treatment of brain abscess (2023).

title: Yellow crystal or blue crystal
lead: Gout crystals are needles and negatively birefringent. Calcium pyrophosphate crystals are rhomboids and positively birefringent.
lines: Parallel to the compensator, gout is yellow and calcium pyrophosphate is blue.
Gout favors the first toe and a previously injured joint. Calcium pyrophosphate favors the knee and the wrist, including the triangular cartilage.
The joint still needs a tap. The history does not replace the crystal.
Needles, negative birefringence, yellow when parallel: urate. Rhomboids, positive, blue: CPPD.
Flare treatment is colchicine, an NSAID, or a glucocorticoid. Allopurinol alone does not treat the hot joint. Continue it if it is already prescribed.
miss: Swapping the colors, or treating a hot knee as gout without looking at the fluid.
diagramAlt: Gout flare drug. Colchicine, NSAID, or glucocorticoid Not allopurinol as the only drug Continue allopurinol if already taking it

source.name: StatPearls. Gout; Calcium Pyrophosphate Deposition Disease.
source.says: Under polarizing microscopy, synovial fluid or tophus aspiration analysis reveals needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals. These crystals are rhomboid or parallelepipedal, as opposed to the strongly negatively birefringent, needle-shaped urate crystals of gout.

more.name: StatPearls. Calcium Pyrophosphate Deposition Disease.
2020 ACR Guideline for the Management of Gout.

title: SJS and TEN are one disease
lead: Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis are the same drug reaction. The name changes with how much skin detaches.
lines: Two or more mucosal surfaces plus skin pain and detachment is the picture. This is not urticaria.
Stop the drug. Care is the care of a burn: fluids, wound care, and a unit that treats this.
The usual drugs are allopurinol, aromatic anticonvulsants, sulfonamides, and some antibiotics. The drug is never given again.
miss: Giving the same drug again because the rash was filed as a simple allergy.

source.name: StatPearls. Stevens-Johnson Syndrome and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis.
source.says: SJS shares the same pathophysiology and is considered part of the same spectrum of drug-induced epidermolysis. SJS affects less than 10% of the total body surface area, SJS and TEN overlap affects 10% to 30% of total body surface area, and TEN affects greater than 30% of total body surface area.

title: Pain out of proportion is a compartment until proved otherwise
lead: Acute compartment syndrome is pain out of proportion and pain on passive stretch. A missing pulse is late, not required.
lines: The usual setup is a fracture, a crush, or a tight cast.
Pain on passive stretch is the early sign. A pulse can still be present.
Measure compartment pressure when the exam is unclear. Pulselessness is late.
Fasciotomy is the treatment. More opioid or overnight observation is not.
miss: Waiting for the pulse to disappear before calling a surgeon.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Compartment Syndrome and Fasciotomy.
source.says: Pain out of proportion to the injury, pain with passive stretch, and paresthesia are the earliest clinical features of acute compartment syndrome. Pallor, pulselessness, and paralysis are late signs, and distal pulses are usually present because systolic pressure exceeds compartment pressure.

more.name: AAOS clinical practice guideline. Management of acute compartment syndrome (2018).

title: Ankylosing spondylitis is better with movement
lead: Ankylosing spondylitis is inflammatory back pain in a young adult. It is worse with rest and better with activity, the opposite of mechanical pain.
lines: HLA-B27 supports it and does not diagnose it.
The spine can fuse. The plain film of the sacroiliac joints is the late picture. MRI sees it earlier.
Uveitis and aortitis travel with it. Ask about the eye.
An NSAID is the first drug for active disease. A painful red eye is seen the same day.
miss: Ordering six weeks of rest for a young man whose stiffness is worst in the morning.

source.name: StatPearls. Ankylosing Spondylitis.
source.says: The presence of inflammatory back pain is characterized by at least 4 of the following 5 features: onset of symptoms before the age of 40, gradual and insidious onset, relief with exercise, lack of improvement with rest, and nocturnal pain with improvement upon arising.

more.name: 2019 ACR/SAA/SPARTAN recommendations for ankylosing spondylitis.

title: Dermatomyositis shows on the hands and the lids
lead: Dermatomyositis is proximal weakness plus Gottron papules or a heliotrope rash. In an adult, look for a cancer.
lines: The weakness is the shoulders and the hips, not the hands first.
Creatine kinase is high. The diagnosis is the muscle and the skin, not the enzyme alone.
Interstitial lung disease travels with some antibodies. Ask about breathlessness.
Adults get a cancer search. Immunosuppression treats the muscle. A statin myopathy has no rash.
miss: Calling the rash eczema and missing the shoulders the patient can no longer lift.

source.name: StatPearls. Dermatomyositis.
source.says: Dermatomyositis is a rare immune-mediated disease characterized by pathognomonic skin findings and symmetric proximal muscle weakness. Heliotrope rash : This characteristic finding presents as a violaceous or erythematous rash affecting the upper eyelids, with or without periorbital edema. Importantly, some subsets of dermatomyositis are associated with a higher risk for malignant neoplasm, making early recognition essential to improving outcomes.

more.name: IMACS international guideline for cancer screening in idiopathic inflammatory myopathy (2023).

title: Giant cell arteritis threatens the eye
lead: Giant cell arteritis in a person over 50 is treated with a high-dose glucocorticoid as soon as it is suspected, about 1 mg/kg of prednisone up to 80 mg, and with an intravenous pulse if vision is threatened.
lines: Start a high-dose glucocorticoid for every suspected case: prednisone about 1 mg/kg, up to 80 mg a day.
If vision is threatened, give an intravenous glucocorticoid pulse rather than tablets alone.
Biopsy as soon as possible, ideally within 2 weeks of starting steroids. A later biopsy can still show arteritis.
Prefer a specimen longer than 1 cm. Do not wait for the sedimentation rate to give the first dose.
miss: Waiting for the biopsy, or for the sedimentation rate, before the first glucocorticoid dose.

source.name: 2021 American College of Rheumatology/Vasculitis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Giant Cell Arteritis and Takayasu Arteritis.
source.says: High dose oral glucocorticoids: prednisone 1 mg/kg up to 80 mg daily. With threatened vision loss, pulse intravenous glucocorticoids are conditionally recommended. A long-segment biopsy (>1 cm) is preferred, obtained within two weeks of starting oral glucocorticoids; a biopsy obtained later could still be informative.

title: Polymyalgia is the girdle, and the muscle enzymes are normal
lead: Polymyalgia rheumatica is bilateral shoulder and hip stiffness in an older adult, with a high sedimentation rate and normal muscle enzymes.
lines: The response to a modest steroid dose is part of the picture.
It is not polymyositis. The enzymes and the biopsy are different.
Ask about headache and vision, because giant cell arteritis can sit beside it.
That normal CK separates it from myositis.
miss: Starting a statin workup or a muscle biopsy for girdle stiffness with a normal creatine kinase.

source.name: StatPearls. Polymyalgia Rheumatica.
source.says: Polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) is a rheumatic disorder characterized by pain and stiffness around the neck, shoulder, and hip area. It is an inflammatory condition associated with an elevation of erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP), being the common findings. Although the patient might complain of nonspecific weakness, muscle strength is usually intact on a more thorough examination.

title: Psoriatic arthritis hits the DIP joint and the nail
lead: Psoriatic arthritis inflames a distal interphalangeal joint, pits the nail, and can swell a whole digit.
lines: The skin psoriasis can be hidden on the scalp or the gluteal cleft, or it can come later.
The x-ray late finding is pencil-in-cup. You do not need it to diagnose a swollen digit.
Rheumatoid arthritis prefers the MCP and the PIP and spares the DIP.
Treat the joint even if the skin is mild. Pencil-in-cup is a late film, not required for the diagnosis.
miss: Calling every hand arthritis rheumatoid because a rheumatoid factor was not ordered yet.

source.name: StatPearls. Psoriatic Arthritis.
source.says: Distal interphalangeal joints are frequently involved in psoriatic arthritis but not rheumatoid arthritis because these joints have many entheses but very little synovial tissue. A severe psoriasis phenotype, scalp, intergluteal, and perianal psoriasis, presence of nail pitting, low level of education, and uveitis predict the development of psoriatic arthritis in patients with psoriasis.

title: Reactive arthritis follows an infection and the joint is sterile
lead: Reactive arthritis is a sterile arthritis days to weeks after a genital or gut infection.
lines: The classic cluster is arthritis, uveitis, and urethritis. Not every patient has all three.
The joint tap is inflammatory and culture-negative.
Treat the triggering infection if it is still present. The arthritis is not septic.
Sterile inflammatory joint days to weeks after Chlamydia or a gut infection. Culture of the fluid is negative.
Treat a still-present infection. Use an NSAID for the joint. Uveitis needs an eye exam the same day.
miss: Operating a culture-negative knee as septic arthritis because the patient had dysuria.

source.name: StatPearls. Reactive Arthritis.
source.says: Reactive arthritis is a sterile inflammatory arthritis that arises following a gastrointestinal or genitourinary tract infection, most frequently triggered by organisms such as Chlamydia trachomatis, Salmonella spp, Shigella spp, Yersinia spp, and Campylobacter spp.

title: Marfan lens goes up, and the aorta is the danger
lead: Marfan syndrome is an FBN1 defect. The protein is fibrillin, and the threat to life is aortic root dilatation.
lines: Inheritance is autosomal dominant, with a reported incidence of about 1 in 3000 to 5000.
Death is usually from aortic root dilatation or dissection.
Lens dislocation and mitral valve prolapse travel with the long skeleton.
miss: Measuring the fingers and never measuring the aortic root.
diagramAlt: Marfan syndrome. FBN1 makes fibrillin Aortic root dilatation is the danger Lens dislocation is the eye finding

source.name: StatPearls. Marfan Syndrome.
source.says: The defect is in the FBN1 gene of chromosome 15, which produces fibrillin, a connective tissue protein. Decreased life expectancy occurs primarily due to aortic complications, including aortic root dilatation and dissection. Ocular findings include lens dislocation, cataracts, myopia, and retinal detachment.

title: Osteogenesis imperfecta is type I collagen
lead: Osteogenesis imperfecta is type I collagen that fails. Blue sclerae, fractures, and hearing loss travel together.
lines: Child abuse also fractures bones. The sclerae, the teeth, and the family history are how you tell them apart, and you still protect the child.
The fractures happen with little force.
Hearing loss is from the same collagen, not a separate ear disease.
Child protection stays open. Blue sclerae do not prove the fracture was accidental, and the two can coexist.
Blue sclerae do not close a child-protection question. Inflicted injury and this disease can both be present.
miss: Diagnosing abuse from one fracture and missing blue sclerae, or diagnosing the disease and missing abuse.

source.name: StatPearls. Osteogenesis Imperfecta.
source.says: Osteogenesis imperfecta is a genetic disorder of connective tissues caused by an abnormality in the synthesis or processing of type I collagen. Clinical features include generalized osteoporosis, increased bone fragility with fractures typically occurring during ambulatory childhood years, blue sclera, conductive hearing loss, and mild short stature.

title: Pemphigus is flaccid and inside the epidermis
lead: Pemphigus vulgaris is flaccid bullae, a positive Nikolsky sign, and antibodies against desmoglein in the epidermis.
lines: The mouth is almost always involved.
Immunofluorescence looks like a net around the cells.
Bullous pemphigoid is the opposite: tense bullae, older adults, and a split under the epidermis.
Systemic corticosteroid plus a steroid-sparing drug. Topical therapy alone does not treat widespread disease.
miss: Swapping pemphigus and pemphigoid because both blister.

source.name: StatPearls. Pemphigus Vulgaris.
source.says: In patients with PV, autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 (Dsg 1) and desmoglein 3 (Dsg 3) is the purported cause. Acantholysis is seen as a result of the autoantibodies destroying the intracellular connections, leading to bullae that can easily rupture (known clinically as the Nikolsky sign).

title: Necrotizing fasciitis is pain past the skin you can see
lead: Necrotizing fasciitis is pain out of proportion, a systemically sick patient, and tissue death under skin that can still look almost normal.
lines: The recommendation is prompt diagnosis and timely effective treatment, not a day of antibiotics to see if the skin improves.
Pain beyond the visible skin, toxicity, and a rising lactate are the clinical clues. Crepitus is not required.
Pain beyond the skin you can see, with toxicity, goes to the operating room the same day. Antibiotics alone are not the plan.
miss: Observing suspected necrotizing fasciitis overnight on antibiotics alone.

source.name: IDSA Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Skin and Soft Tissue Infections: 2014 Update.
source.says: Prompt surgical consultation is recommended for aggressive infections with systemic toxicity or suspected necrotizing fasciitis or gas gangrene (strong). Empiric antibiotics should be broad, e.g., vancomycin or linezolid plus piperacillin-tazobactam or a carbapenem.

title: Cellulitis is the dermis, and erysipelas has a sharp edge
lead: Cellulitis is a dermal infection with edges that fade. Erysipelas is more superficial, raised, and sharply demarcated.
lines: Group A streptococcus and Staphylococcus aureus are the organisms.
A purulent, drainable collection is an abscess and needs drainage, not a longer course of the same pill.
Mark the border. Spread beyond the mark is treatment failure.
Flat, indistinct borders: cellulitis, usually group A strep or staph. Raised, sharp border: erysipelas.
miss: Incising flat cellulitis, or treating a drainable abscess with pills alone.

source.name: StatPearls. Cellulitis.
source.says: Compared with erysipelas, which has sharply defined borders and superficial involvement, cellulitis affects deeper tissues and is less clearly defined. Cellulitis is an acute bacterial infection causing inflammation of the deep dermis and surrounding subcutaneous tissue.

title: Which maneuver makes the murmur louder
lead: Less preload softens almost every murmur. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and mitral valve prolapse get louder or longer.
lines: Standing and Valsalva drop preload. Squatting and passive leg raise raise it.
Handgrip raises afterload, so mitral and aortic regurgitation and a VSD get louder, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy gets softer.
Inspiration increases right-sided murmurs. Expiration increases left-sided murmurs.
miss: Calling every murmur that gets louder with Valsalva aortic stenosis.
diagramAlt: Preload down, from standing or Valsalva, softens most murmurs and makes hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and mitral valve prolapse louder or longer. Handgrip makes regurgitant murmurs louder and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy softer.

source.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Cardiovascular Murmurs.
source.says: Valsalva : Decreases preload. Valsalva increases the strength of murmurs due to hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy and mitral valve prolapse. Squatting increases the intensity of aortic stenosis, mitral stenosis, aortic regurgitation, and mitral regurgitation.

title: Use dependence versus reverse use dependence
lead: Class I sodium blockers bind harder at fast rates. Pure class III potassium blockers bind harder at slow rates.
lines: Class III blocks potassium channels and prolongs repolarization. Sotalol and dofetilide show reverse use dependence, so the QT risk is greatest when the rate is slow.
Class II and class IV slow the AV node. They are not the drugs that prolong the QRS.
Class I sodium blockers bind open channels and work harder at fast rates. Class Ic is the most use-dependent.
miss: Treating every class III drug as if it worked better during tachycardia.

source.name: StatPearls. Antiarrhythmic Medications.
source.says: Antiarrhythmic medications play a pivotal role in managing various cardiac rhythm disorders, and their classification under the Vaughan-Williams system serves as a cornerstone for understanding their diverse mechanisms of action.

title: What the microscope shows after an infarct
lead: Neutrophils dominate days 1 to 3. Macrophages clear dead muscle on days 3 to 7, and that is when the wall ruptures.
lines: The first day is early coagulation necrosis. Neutrophils are not the story yet.
Days 3 to 7 are the rupture window: free wall, septum, or papillary muscle.
A firm collagen scar takes weeks. Reperfusion can add hemorrhage, but it does not move the rupture window to the first hour.
miss: Dating a rupture to the afternoon of the infarct, or dating neutrophils to week three.
diagramAlt: Infarct histology. Day 0–1: coagulation, few neutrophils Days 1–3: neutrophils Days 3–7: macrophages, rupture risk

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Myocardial Infarction.
source.says: At 12 to 24 hours, the gross specimen appears dark and mottled, with contraction band necrosis and neutrophil predominance observed on histopathology. Subsequently, nuclei reduction occurs between 1 to 3 days, and then, within the next 3 to 7 days, macrophages emerge to clear apoptotic cells.

title: Tamponade equalizes diastolic pressures
lead: Cardiac tamponade equalizes diastolic pressures and drops the y descent. The clue at the bedside is pulsus paradoxus and a quiet heart.
lines: Beck's triad is low pressure, distended neck veins, and muffled sounds. Not every patient has all three.
Electrical alternans is the heart swinging in fluid.
Diastolic pressures equalize and the y descent drops. Pulsus paradoxus is an exaggerated inspiratory fall in systolic pressure.
Fluids are a bridge. Drainage is the treatment. A diuretic removes the last preload.
miss: Giving a diuretic for distended neck veins and dropping the last preload the heart had.

source.name: StatPearls. Cardiac Tamponade.
source.says: Patients present with dyspnea, chest discomfort, hypotension, elevated jugular venous pressure, muffled heart sounds, and pulsus paradoxus. The presence of pulsus paradoxus, defined as a decrease in systolic blood pressure exceeding 10 mm Hg during inspiration, supports the diagnosis of cardiac tamponade.

title: Aortic dissection is a tear, and the pressures do not match
lead: Aortic dissection is a tearing chest pain into the back. The arm pressures or the pulses do not match.
lines: A widened mediastinum supports it. A normal chest film does not exclude it.
Type A involves the ascending aorta and goes to the operating room.
Thrombolysis for a mistaken myocardial infarction extends the tear.
Unequal arm pressures or pulses and tearing pain to the back. Give a beta blocker before a pure vasodilator.
Involvement of the ascending aorta is an operation. A fibrinolytic extends the tear.
miss: Giving a lytic for chest pain before the pulses and the mediastinum are considered.
diagramAlt: Ascending dissection. Beta blocker before a pure vasodilator Type A: operating room No fibrinolytic

source.name: StatPearls. Aortic Dissection.
source.says: While the classic presentation of acute aortic dissection involves sudden, severe, “tearing” chest pain, subtle presentations often lead to missed diagnoses. Blood pressure discrepancies greater than 20 mm Hg between arms, a pulse deficit, or wide pulse pressure are red flags in the physical exam.

more.name: 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease.

title: A pulsatile mass in a smoker is an aneurysm until imaged
lead: An abdominal aortic aneurysm is a disease of older people who smoked. A pulsatile mass and hypotension with back pain is rupture.
lines: Do not repeatedly palpate a tender aneurysm.
The screen in the right patient is an ultrasound, once.
The rupture goes to the operating room or the endovascular suite, not to a clinic follow-up.
Rupture is back or abdominal pain plus hypotension. That patient goes to repair, not to a clinic ultrasound.
One-time ultrasound screening for AAA in men aged 65 to 75 years who have ever smoked.
miss: Sending a hypotensive older smoker with back pain for outpatient ultrasound tomorrow.
diagramAlt: Who gets one AAA ultrasound. Men 65–75 who have ever smoked One ultrasound, not yearly Rupture: back pain + hypotension, not a clinic scan

source.name: StatPearls. Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
source.says: Risk factors for AAAs include atherosclerosis (the most common), smoking, advanced age, male sex, White race, family history of AAA, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and prior history of aortic dissection. Palpation of the abdomen usually reveals a nontender, pulsatile abdominal mass.

more.name: USPSTF. Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: Screening.

title: Dilated cardiomyopathy fails in systole
lead: Dilated cardiomyopathy is a weak, enlarged ventricle. The failure is systolic, and an S3 is the sound.
lines: Alcohol, doxorubicin, and a viral myocarditis are the classic causes you can name.
The coronary arteries can be clean. Ischemia is a different dilated heart.
The ejection fraction is low. Preserved-ejection-fraction failure is the other disease.
If alcohol is the cause, stopping it is the disease-modifying order. A low EF still gets the four-drug HFrEF regimen.
miss: Calling every heart failure ischemic without asking about alcohol and the ejection fraction.

source.name: StatPearls. Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
source.says: By definition, patients have systolic dysfunction and may or may not have overt symptoms of heart failure. Findings include crackles in the lung fields, elevated jugular venous pressures, peripheral edema, and an S3 gallop.

title: Restrictive cardiomyopathy fills badly and squeezes normally
lead: Restrictive cardiomyopathy is a stiff ventricle with a normal or near-normal ejection fraction. Amyloid is the prototype.
lines: Low voltage on the ECG with a thick ventricle on the image is amyloid.
Hemochromatosis is another infiltrative cause and is a systemic disease.
Constriction from the pericardium can look the same at the bedside and is separated by imaging.
Digoxin binds amyloid and is used cautiously. Look for light chains before raising the diuretic again.
A pericardial knock and a calcification favor constriction over myocardial restriction.
miss: Treating a low-voltage thick heart as ordinary hypertensive hypertrophy.

source.name: StatPearls. Restrictive Cardiomyopathy.
source.says: Cardiac amyloidosis is the most common cause of restrictive cardiomyopathy in developed countries. It is important to suspect RCM in any patient with a normal or close to normal systolic function and evidence of diastolic dysfunction with a restrictive filling pattern on echocardiogram.

title: Endocarditis on a normal valve is staph until proved otherwise
lead: Acute endocarditis on a normal valve is Staphylococcus aureus. Subacute endocarditis on an abnormal valve is viridans streptococci.
lines: Janeway lesions are painless spots on the palms and soles. Osler nodes hurt.
Duke criteria need blood cultures drawn before antibiotics when the patient is stable enough.
A stroke plus a fever plus a murmur is this disease until the echo says otherwise.
Three culture sets from separate sites before antibiotics if the patient is stable. Prophylaxis is only for the highest-risk hearts, not for an isolated click.
miss: Starting antibiotics and then trying to culture the blood.
diagramAlt: Endocarditis cultures. Three sets, separate sticks Before antibiotics if the patient can wait Prophylaxis only for the highest-risk hearts

source.name: StatPearls. Infective Endocarditis.
source.says: Collectively, these groups account for 80% to 90% of all cases, with Staphylococcus aureus alone responsible for about 30% of cases in developed countries. Notably, S aureus demonstrates a predilection for infecting structurally normal native valves, particularly the tricuspid valve. Although fairly uncommon in healthcare-associated infections, viridans group streptococci account for approximately 20% of community-acquired cases.

more.name: 2015 AHA Scientific Statement. Infective endocarditis in adults.

title: Rheumatic heart disease follows an untreated strep throat
lead: Rheumatic heart disease is immune mimicry after group A streptococcus. The valve it damages most often is the mitral valve.
lines: Jones criteria diagnose acute rheumatic fever, not the chronic valve.
The chronic lesion is years later: stenosis, regurgitation, or both.
Prevent the next attack with penicillin in a patient who has already had rheumatic fever.
miss: Treating the sore throat after the valve is already stenotic and calling that prevention.
diagramAlt: Rheumatic prophylaxis. After rheumatic fever: scheduled penicillin Duration depends on carditis One 10-day course is not prophylaxis

source.name: StatPearls. Rheumatic Heart Disease.
source.says: Rheumatic heart disease is the result of valvular damage caused by an abnormal immune response to Streptococcus pyogenes infection, which is classified as a group A streptococcus that causes acute rheumatic fever. In chronic rheumatic heart disease, the mitral valve alone is the most commonly affected valve in an estimated 50% to 60% of cases.

title: Tetralogy is a boot and a spell that squatting fixes
lead: Tetralogy of Fallot is pulmonic stenosis, right ventricular hypertrophy, an overriding aorta, and a ventricular septal defect.
lines: A spell is infundibular spasm. Squatting raises systemic resistance and pushes blood to the lungs.
The chest film is a boot-shaped heart with less pulmonary blood flow.
The murmur of the stenosis gets softer during a spell, because less blood crosses the valve.
Knees-to-chest raises systemic resistance and sends blood to the lungs. A vasodilator does the opposite. The murmur gets softer as less blood crosses the valve.
miss: Giving something that drops systemic resistance during a spell and worsening the shunt.
diagramAlt: Hypercyanotic spell. Knees to chest. Oxygen. Calm Raise systemic resistance A vasodilator worsens the right-to-left shunt

source.name: StatPearls. Tetralogy of Fallot.
source.says: Classic tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) is a congenital heart defect (CHD) that is comprised of 4 anatomical alterations: a large, anteriorly malaligned ventricular septal defect (VSD), an overriding aorta which results in infundibular (ie, sub-pulmonary) right ventricular outflow tract obstruction (RVOTO), and consequent right ventricular hypertrophy secondary to chronic systemic pressures.

title: Coarctation is a blood pressure the legs do not share
lead: Coarctation of the aorta raises the pressure in the arms above the pressure in the legs and delays the femoral pulse.
lines: Rib notching is collateral flow, a late film finding.
Turner syndrome is the association. Check the karyotype in a girl.
A bicuspid aortic valve often sits with it. Listen for the click.
miss: Diagnosing essential hypertension in a young adult without comparing the arms and the legs.

source.name: StatPearls. Coarctation of the Aorta.
source.says: The hallmark of aortic coarctation is a significant difference in blood pressure between the upper and lower extremities; therefore, a physical examination will often reveal elevated blood pressure in the upper extremities and diminished or delayed femoral pulses compared to brachial or radial pulses, known as brachiofemoral delay.

title: Preserved ejection fraction is a filling problem
lead: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is a ventricle that does not fill well. The squeeze is 50% or higher.
lines: The patient is still congested. A normal ejection fraction does not mean the dyspnea is anxiety.
Hypertension, age, and obesity are the usual setup.
A low ejection fraction is the other heart failure and uses the four-drug regimen of reduced ejection fraction.
Ejection fraction at least 50% with congestion. The problem is filling, not a globally weak squeeze.
An SGLT2 inhibitor has a recommendation. Do not copy carvedilol, an MRA, and an ARNI onto every preserved-EF admission.
miss: Stopping the workup because the ejection fraction was reported as normal.
diagramAlt: HFpEF versus HFrEF. HFpEF: EF ≥50%, filling problem SGLT2 inhibitor has a recommendation Do not copy all four HFrEF drugs blindly

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: HFpEF (HF with preserved EF): LVEF ≥50%, with evidence of spontaneous or provokable increased LV filling pressures (e.g., elevated natriuretic peptide, noninvasive and invasive hemodynamic measurement).

title: Typical flutter uses the cavotricuspid isthmus
lead: Typical atrial flutter is a macro-reentry loop that must pass through the cavotricuspid isthmus. The ECG is a sawtooth.
lines: The ventricular rate is often 150 when the node conducts 2 to 1.
Anticoagulation follows the same stroke logic as fibrillation when the risk is high.
Typical flutter is cavotricuspid-isthmus macro-reentry. A ventricular rate of 150 with sawtooth waves is 2:1 conduction.
Ablation of the isthmus treats the circuit. Stroke prevention follows the same risk threshold as fibrillation and is not cancelled by sinus rhythm.
miss: Calling every regular narrow tachycardia sinus tachycardia because the rate is 150.

source.name: StatPearls. Atrial Flutter.
source.says: Typical or cavotricuspid isthmus (CTI) dependent is the most common type of atrial flutter; this rhythm originates in the right atrium at the level of the tricuspid valve annulus. In inferior leads, typical flutter waves resemble a picket fence or sawtooth because the P waves are negative due to the direction of the vector.

more.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for Atrial Fibrillation.

title: A long QT is a pause that starts torsades
lead: A prolonged QT sets up torsades de pointes, a polymorphic ventricular tachycardia that follows a pause.
lines: Potassium and magnesium being low, and drugs that block the potassium current, make it longer.
The acute drug for torsades is intravenous magnesium, even when the serum magnesium is normal.
A congenital long QT is a family history of sudden death and a QT you measure, not guess.
Stop the QT-prolonging drug. Do not give amiodarone or another QT-prolonging antiarrhythmic for torsades.
miss: Treating torsades with a drug that prolongs the QT further.

source.name: StatPearls. Torsade de Pointes.
source.says: Torsades de pointes is a form of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia characterized on an electrocardiogram by gradual changes in QRS-complex amplitude and a twisting pattern around the isoelectric line.
