The onset of Torsades de Pointes is often preceded by a run of short-long-short R-R intervals.

more.name: 2022 ESC guidelines for ventricular arrhythmias and the prevention of sudden cardiac death.

title: Mitral valve prolapse clicks in mid-systole
lead: Mitral valve prolapse is a mid-systolic click and a late systolic murmur. More preload makes the click later.
lines: Most leaflets that prolapse a little are benign.
A connective-tissue disease is the question when the prolapse is severe or the aorta is involved.
The maneuver that lengthens the murmur is less preload, not more.
Standing and Valsalva drop preload: most murmurs soften, HCM and MVP get louder or longer.
Handgrip raises afterload: mitral and aortic regurgitation get louder, HCM gets softer. Inspiration increases right-sided murmurs.
miss: Hearing a click and diagnosing papillary-muscle rupture. Rupture is a holosystolic murmur and shock after an infarct.
diagramAlt: Less preload. Most murmurs soften HCM and MVP get louder or longer Handgrip: regurgitation louder, HCM softer

source.name: StatPearls. Mitral Valve Prolapse.
source.says: The classic auscultated murmur in MVP is a mid-systolic click followed by a late-systolic murmur.

title: A normal anion gap asks the urine
lead: When the anion gap is normal, urine sodium plus potassium minus chloride tells you if the kidney is answering with ammonium.
lines: A negative urine anion gap means the kidney is excreting acid. The bicarbonate was lost from the gut.
A positive urine anion gap means the kidney is not answering. That is a renal tubular acidosis.
The serum anion gap uses sodium, chloride, and bicarbonate. The urine calculation does not.
miss: Calling every normal-gap acidosis diarrhea without checking the urine electrolytes.
diagramAlt: Urine anion gap equals urine sodium plus potassium minus chloride. Negative means the kidney is excreting acid. Positive means a renal tubular acidosis.

source.name: StatPearls. Anion Gap and Non-Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis.
source.says: In nonanion gap metabolic acidosis, gastrointestinal and renal losses of bicarbonate can be distinguished via urine anion gap analysis: Urine anion gap = Urine Na + Urine K – Urine Cl, if urine pH is <6.5. The urine anion gap can help estimate the urinary ammonium.

title: Nephritic sediment versus nephrotic protein
lead: Nephritic urine has red cells and red-cell casts. Nephrotic urine has heavy protein, at least 3.5 g a day.
lines: Nephritic disease also brings oliguria and hypertension. IgA nephropathy is the common prototype and the blood is often during or just after a mucosal infection.
Nephrotic disease brings low albumin, edema, and high lipids. Minimal change disease is the prototype in children: selective albumin loss and foot-process effacement.
Some diseases do both. Do not force a mixed picture into one column.
miss: Treating every swollen patient as nephrotic, or calling IgA post-streptococcal because both follow a sore throat.

source.name: StatPearls. IgA Nephropathy (Berger Disease). Minimal Change Disease.
source.says: The presence of red cells and red cell casts indicates glomerular injury and potential active disease. A spot protein/creatinine ratio greater than 200 mg/mmol in children and protein/creatinine ratio>300-350mg/mmol in adults is consistent with nephrotic syndrome, as is a 24-hour urine collection that reveals a total protein greater than 3 to 3.5 g/24hour in adults.

more.name: StatPearls. Minimal Change Disease.

title: Where each diuretic works
lead: Loops block NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb and waste calcium. Thiazides block NCC in the distal tubule and save calcium.
lines: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors act in the proximal tubule and cause a metabolic acidosis.
Loops and thiazides both cause a metabolic alkalosis. Loops also waste magnesium and can hurt hearing.
Spironolactone and eplerenone block aldosterone. Amiloride blocks ENaC. Both save potassium.
miss: Using a loop when the goal is to lower urine calcium, or starting a potassium-sparing drug and never checking the potassium.
diagramAlt: Nephron map. Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors in the proximal tubule. Loops on the thick ascending limb. Thiazides on the distal convoluted tubule. Potassium-sparing drugs on the collecting duct.

source.name: StatPearls. Loop Diuretics. Thiazide Diuretics.
source.says: Loop diuretics induce its effect by competing with chloride to bind to the Na-K-2Cl (NKCC2) cotransporter at the apical membrane of the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle and blocking the cotransporter, which inhibits the reabsorption of sodium and chloride. Blocking of the NKCC2 cotransporter makes potassium unable to be reabsorbed back into the lumen, which results in the loss of calcium and magnesium ions. Thiazides reduce urine calcium levels and increase blood calcium by increasing calcium reabsorption from the luminal membrane into the interstitium in exchange for sodium.

more.name: StatPearls. Thiazide Diuretics.

title: Why the oxygen saturation did not rise
lead: A true shunt does not correct on 100% oxygen. Hypoventilation and low inspired oxygen keep a normal A-a gradient.
lines: The five causes of hypoxemia are low inspired oxygen, hypoventilation, diffusion limitation, V/Q mismatch, and shunt.
Diffusion limitation, V/Q mismatch, and shunt widen the A-a gradient.
A right-shifted curve unloads oxygen: higher CO2, higher H+, higher 2,3-BPG, higher temperature. Carbon monoxide shifts the curve left and drops the oxygen content while PaO2 stays normal.
miss: Giving more oxygen for a shunt and expecting the saturation to normalize, or reading a normal PaO2 as proof against carbon monoxide.
diagramAlt: Hypoxemia split. Normal A-a gradient: low inspired oxygen or hypoventilation. High A-a gradient: V/Q mismatch, diffusion limitation, or shunt. Shunt does not correct on 100 percent oxygen.

source.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Alveolar to Arterial Oxygen Gradient; Hypoxia and Hypoxemia.
source.says: Thus patients with hypoxemia due to hypoventilation will have an A-a gradient within normal limits. Thus patients with hypoxemia due to pneumonia will have an inappropriately elevated A-a gradient. Failure of PaO2 to normalize despite administration of 100% oxygen is the defining physiologic feature distinguishing true shunting from V/Q mismatch.

more.name: StatPearls. Hypoxia and Hypoxemia.

title: COPD is an FEV1/FVC that does not come back
lead: COPD is airflow obstruction that does not fully reverse. The ratio of FEV1 to FVC stays below 0.70 after a bronchodilator.
lines: GOLD diagnoses obstruction with a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.70. Do not call it COPD from cough alone.
A large bronchodilator response points back toward asthma.
Long-term oxygen is for a resting PaO2 at or under 55 mm Hg, or a saturation at or under 88%.
That oxygen, not an extra inhaler, is the therapy tied to survival in chronic hypoxemia.
miss: Diagnosing COPD from a smoker’s cough without spirometry.

source.name: GOLD 2027 Report. Global Strategy for Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD.
source.says: The presence of non-fully reversible airflow obstruction (FEV1/FVC < 0.7 post-bronchodilation) measured by spirometry confirms the diagnosis of COPD. Long-term oxygen is indicated for stable COPD with PaO2 at or below 55 mmHg (7.3 kPa) or SaO2 at or below 88%.

title: Tension pneumothorax shifts the trachea away
lead: Tension pneumothorax is a one-way valve. The trachea shifts away from the silent side, and the shock is obstructive.
lines: Breath sounds are absent on the injured side, and the neck veins are distended.
The treatment is decompression, then a chest tube. A chest film is for a stable patient.
The shock is obstructive, from compressed venous return, not from blood lost into the chest.
miss: Ordering a film on a patient whose pressure is falling and whose trachea has already moved.

source.name: StatPearls. Tension Pneumothorax.
source.says: Tension pneumothorax arises when air accumulation becomes sufficient to compress the mediastinum and shift it contralaterally. Tracheal deviation and mediastinal shift toward the contralateral side may be evident. A rapid, focused examination typically reveals severe respiratory distress, hypotension, and an enlarged, hyperresonant hemithorax with absent breath sounds. Clinical diagnosis hinges on signs like hypotension, unilateral breath sounds, distended neck veins, and tracheal deviation.

title: ARDS is wet lungs and a left atrium that is not the cause
lead: The acute respiratory distress syndrome is bilateral infiltrates and hypoxemia that heart failure does not explain.
lines: The lung is stiff. Compliance is low.
The ratio of arterial oxygen to inspired oxygen grades the severity.
The tidal volume that injures less is about 6 mL per kilogram of predicted body weight, and the plateau pressure stays at or under 30.
Bilateral infiltrates not explained by left-atrial pressure. Tidal volume 6 mL/kg predicted body weight from height and sex.
Plateau pressure at or under 30 cm H2O. A PaCO2 of 50 can be accepted. Do not use actual body weight.
miss: Ventilating an ARDS patient on actual body weight and calling a prettier saturation a success.
diagramAlt: ARDS tidal volume. 6 mL/kg predicted body weight Use height and sex, not the scale Plateau pressure ≤30 cm H2O

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
source.says: According to the Berlin definition, ARDS is defined by acute onset, bilateral lung infiltrates on chest radiography or CT scan of a non-cardiac origin, and a PaO2/FiO2 ratio of less than 300 mm Hg.

more.name: ARDS Network. Ventilation with lower tidal volumes. N Engl J Med (2000).

title: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis crackles at the bases
lead: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is usual interstitial pneumonia: basilar and peripheral fibrosis, honeycombing, and Velcro crackles.
lines: The clubbing and the dry cough in an older adult are the bedside pair.
A steroid is not disease-modifying the way students were taught. Antifibrotic drugs are the current conversation.
Basal, peripheral honeycombing and Velcro crackles. Exclude connective-tissue disease and exposures before calling it idiopathic.
Nintedanib or pirfenidone is the disease-modifying choice. Long-term prednisone is not that treatment.
miss: Treating every dry crackle with weeks of prednisone as if it were sarcoid.
diagramAlt: IPF drug. Nintedanib or pirfenidone Not long-term prednisone as the disease drug Oxygen if hypoxemic

source.name: StatPearls. Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
source.says: Classic pulmonary findings include fine bibasilar velcro crackles heard during inspiration. Differentiating usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP), a radiologic and histopathologic pattern, from IPF is essential. Bronchoscopic biopsy yields are typically low as the pathologic changes start subpleurally.

more.name: ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT Clinical Practice Guideline. Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (2022).

title: Bronchiectasis is a permanently wide airway full of sputum
lead: Bronchiectasis is irreversible dilation of bronchi. The patient coughs cups of sputum.
lines: Cystic fibrosis, a prior severe infection, and immune defects are the causes to name.
The CT is the tram tracks and the signet ring, not a normal film.
Daily airway clearance is the treatment of the anatomy. Antibiotics treat a flare or a cultured Pseudomonas, not the dilated bronchi.
miss: Calling recurrent pneumonia ordinary asthma because the patient wheezes.

source.name: StatPearls. Bronchiectasis.
source.says: Bronchial dilation, the cardinal sign of bronchiectasis. Cough: 98%, sputum: 78% (sputum is typically mucoid and relatively odorless), dyspnea: 62%.

more.name: ERS clinical practice guideline for the management of adult bronchiectasis.

title: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is the place the patient breathes
lead: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is an immune reaction to an inhaled antigen. The farmer, the bird owner, and the hot-tub user are the histories.
lines: Acute disease is hours after exposure and looks like a flu with crackles.
Chronic disease scars the upper and mid lungs.
Name and remove the inhaled antigen. Immunosuppression without removal does not treat hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
miss: Adding another inhaler and never asking about birds.

source.name: StatPearls. Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis.
source.says: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is an immune-mediated interstitial lung disease that develops in susceptible individuals after inhalation of one or more inciting antigens. These include agriculture, animal care, manufacturing, woodworking, gardening, using hot tubs, and contact with mold, birds, feathers, or contaminated water systems.

more.name: ATS/JRS/ALAT guideline. Diagnosis of hypersensitivity pneumonitis in adults (2020).

title: The distal tubule that cannot acidify is type 1
lead: Type 1 renal tubular acidosis cannot acidify the urine. Potassium is low, and calcium stones form.
lines: Type 2 is a proximal leak. The urine can still acidify once bicarbonate is low, and Fanconi features may be present.
Type 4 is the hyperkalemic one, from low aldosterone effect.
All three can lower bicarbonate. The potassium and the urine pH separate them.
miss: Calling every non-gap acidosis diarrhea. Diarrhea also lowers potassium, and the urine anion gap is the separator.
diagramAlt: Renal tubular acidosis and K. Type 1 distal: low K, urine pH >5.5 Type 2 proximal: low K, can acidify later Type 4: high K, low aldosterone effect

source.name: StatPearls. Renal Tubular Acidosis.
source.says: This raises the pH of urine due to an inability to excrete acid and generate acidic urine in the distal tubule, even in states of metabolic acidosis. It is associated with hypokalemia due to the failure of H/K ATPase. These patients can develop hypercalciuria, hypocitraturia, and nephrolithiasis.

title: Hypernatremia is a water deficit
lead: Hypernatremia is too little water for the sodium. The patient is thirsty if the thirst mechanism works.
lines: Correct the water slowly. A fast drop in sodium swells the brain that has adapted.
Diabetes insipidus makes dilute urine in the face of a high serum osmolality.
Dehydration from poor access to water makes concentrated urine. The urine tells you which.
Concentrated urine means the kidney is holding water and intake was the problem. Dilute urine is diabetes insipidus.
miss: Replacing the entire deficit with free water in a few hours.
diagramAlt: Hypernatremia pace. Free-water deficit, replaced slowly Recheck sodium. Do not drop it overnight Desmopressin only if central DI

source.name: StatPearls. Hypernatremia.
source.says: The basic mechanisms of hypernatremia are water deficit and excess solute. The human body maintains sodium and water homeostasis by concentrating the urine secondary to the action of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) and increased fluid intake by a powerful thirst response.

title: Severe hypokalemia is a potassium under 2.5
lead: The chapter's floor for a normal serum potassium is about 3.5 mmol/L, and a value under 2.5 mmol/L is severe.
lines: 3 to 3.4 mmol/L is mild, 2.5 to 3 is moderate, and under 2.5 mmol/L is severe.
Weakness, cramps, and palpitations follow the severity. Arrhythmia is the severe risk.
The serum value is a small fraction of body stores, so it does not measure total potassium.
miss: Calling a potassium of 2.4 mmol/L mild, or judging total body stores from the serum value alone.
diagramAlt: Hypokalemia severity. Floor about 3.5 mmol/L Mild 3 to 3.4; moderate 2.5 to 3 Severe: under 2.5 mmol/L

source.name: StatPearls. Hypokalemia.
source.says: Although variation exists, an acceptable lower limit for normal serum potassium is 3.5 mmol/L. Serum potassium levels less than 2.5 mmol/L are classified as severe.

title: A low calcium prolongs the QT and twitches the face
lead: Hypocalcemia prolongs the QT and makes Chvostek and Trousseau signs. The muscle is irritable, not weak from potassium.
lines: After the parathyroid glands are removed, the calcium falls within a day or two.
Low magnesium keeps the parathyroid from releasing hormone. Replace it.
Calcium gluconate is the acute drug when the QT is long or the patient is seizing.
Prolonged QT, Chvostek or Trousseau sign, tetany, or a seizure gets intravenous calcium. Recheck magnesium.
miss: Treating a long QT with magnesium only, when the calcium was the ion that fell.
diagramAlt: Symptomatic hypocalcemia. Long QT, tetany, or seizure: IV calcium Check magnesium with it Post-thyroidectomy: scheduled calcium checks

source.name: StatPearls. Hypocalcemia.
source.says: QTc prolongation: A cardiac manifestation that may predispose to torsades de pointes. Chvostek sign: Another manifestation of increased neuromuscular excitability, elicited by tapping over the facial nerve anterior to the ear. Carpopedal spasm (Trousseau sign): Reflects increased neuromuscular excitability.

title: Vomiting makes a chloride-responsive alkalosis
lead: Metabolic alkalosis from vomiting loses acid and volume. The urine chloride is low, and saline corrects it.
lines: A diuretic does the same while the patient is still volume-down.
A high urine chloride means the kidney is generating the alkalosis, as in hyperaldosteronism. Saline will not fix that.
Potassium is low in both. The urine chloride is the split.
That is vomiting or a recent diuretic.
miss: Pouring saline into a hypertensive patient whose urine chloride is already high.

source.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Metabolic Alkalosis.
source.says: Therefore, the large volume loss of gastric secretions will correlate with a loss of hydrogen chloride, an acidic substance, leading to a relative increase in bicarbonate in the blood, thus driving alkalosis. Metabolic alkalosis is split into 2 main categories: Chloride responsive with urine chloride less than 10 mEq/L and chloride resistant with urine chloride greater than 20 mEq/L.

title: Respiratory acidosis is a ventilation problem
lead: Respiratory acidosis is a high PaCO2 from not ventilating. The kidney raises bicarbonate later, not in the first hour.
lines: A sedative, a neuromuscular disease, and an obstructed airway are the causes.
Oxygen does not blow off CO2. Ventilation does.
Noninvasive ventilation is first if the airway is protected and the patient is not in shock.
miss: Giving more oxygen as the treatment of a rising CO2 in a patient who is not breathing.
diagramAlt: When to start NIV. COPD flare with low pH and high CO2 Patient must protect the airway Oxygen alone does not clear CO2

source.name: StatPearls. Respiratory Acidosis.
source.says: In the presence of alveolar hypoventilation, 2 features commonly seen are respiratory acidosis and hypercapnia. In chronic respiratory acidosis, renal compensation occurs gradually over the course of days.

title: SIADH is euvolemic and the urine is concentrated
lead: The syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone is euvolemic hyponatremia with urine that is not dilute.
lines: Uric acid is low. The patient is not edematous and not dry.
Fluid restriction is the first treatment when symptoms are mild.
A seizure from a low sodium is hypertonic saline, not a fluid restriction order written for tomorrow.
Normal saline can lower the sodium further. Fluid restriction for mild symptoms. Hypertonic saline for seizures.
miss: Giving normal saline to SIADH and watching the sodium fall further.

source.name: StatPearls. Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion.
source.says: SIADH is characterized by impaired water excretion leading to hyponatremia with hypervolemia or euvolemia. Urine osmolality greater than 100 mOsm/kg.

title: Diabetes insipidus makes water and cannot hold it
lead: Diabetes insipidus is dilute urine while the serum is concentrated. Desmopressin raises the urine concentration if the problem is central.
lines: Nephrogenic disease does not answer to desmopressin. Lithium is the classic cause.
The patient is polyuric, not oliguric.
Psychogenic water drinking dilutes the serum. The urine is dilute and the serum sodium is low or low-normal, not high.
miss: Restricting water in a patient whose sodium is already high and whose urine is water.

source.name: StatPearls. Arginine Vasopressin Disorder (Diabetes Insipidus).
source.says: The hallmarks of diabetes insipidus (DI) include polyuria (>50 mL/kg), dilute urine (osmolality <300 mOsm/L), and increased thirst. After water deprivation, studies have demonstrated that desmopressin can increase urine osmolality by greater than 100% in complete central DI and up to 50% in partial central DI.

title: Renal artery stenosis is a high-renin hypertension
lead: Renal artery stenosis turns on renin. Fibromuscular dysplasia is the young woman. Atherosclerosis is the older smoker.
lines: An ACE inhibitor can crash the filtration when both kidneys, or a single kidney, depend on the stenosis.
A bruit and a rising creatinine after the ACE inhibitor are the clues.
Opening the artery is not automatic. The young fibromuscular lesion is the one that often benefits.
miss: Starting an ACE inhibitor in a solitary-kidney stenosis and not rechecking the creatinine.

source.name: StatPearls. Renal Artery Stenosis.
source.says: In patients with renal artery stenosis, chronic ischemia from renal blood flow obstruction leads to adaptive changes in the kidney, including the formation of collateral blood vessels and renin secretion by the juxtaglomerular apparatus. Atherosclerotic disease accounts for the vast majority of cases, typically affecting older adults with generalized vascular disease, whereas fibromuscular dysplasia more commonly affects younger individuals.

title: Adult polycystic kidneys bring hypertension and aneurysms
lead: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease makes big cystic kidneys, hypertension, and berry aneurysms.
lines: The liver can be cystic too. The spleen story is a different disease.
Hematuria after a minor hit is a cyst that bled, and it is still this disease.
A family history plus bilateral cysts is the diagnosis. A biopsy is not the test.
Autosomal dominant disease: bilateral cysts, hypertension, and intracranial aneurysms. Do not biopsy to diagnose it.
A thunderclap headache is imaged the same day. Autosomal recessive disease is the infantile form with congenital hepatic fibrosis.
miss: Biopsying a cystic kidney, or ignoring a sudden headache in a patient with this disease.

source.name: StatPearls. Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
source.says: Hypertension is the most universal and earliest clinical presentation in most patients with ADPKD. A ruptured cerebral aneurysm is the most serious extrarenal complication of ADPKD and has a four times higher prevalence in ADPKD patients compared to the general population.

title: Uric acid stones are invisible on a plain film
lead: Uric acid stones do not show on a plain radiograph. They form in acidic urine, and alkalinizing the urine dissolves them.
lines: A low-purine pattern and a high uric acid are the setup, including tumor lysis.
Calcium stones are the common radiopaque ones. Do not assume every stone is calcium.
The CT still sees the uric acid stone. The plain film does not.
Plain films miss uric acid stones.
Allopurinol is not the acute pain drug.
miss: Telling a patient the stone is gone because the abdominal film is clear.

source.name: StatPearls. Uric Acid Nephrolithiasis.
source.says: Uric acid stones are radiolucent, while calcium-based stones are radioopaque. The most significant risk factor for uric acid stones is acidic urine, often associated with low urinary ammonia levels. Overall, urinary alkalinization is considered the single most effective therapy.

more.name: AUA guideline. Medical management of kidney stones (2014).

title: CKD mineral disease raises phosphate and PTH
lead: In chronic kidney disease the phosphate rises, the calcium falls or sits low-normal, and PTH rises to compensate.
lines: Active vitamin D falls because the kidney cannot hydroxylate it.
A phosphate binder is taken with food. A binder in an empty stomach does nothing.
The early eGFR dip from an SGLT2 inhibitor is a different, expected change and is not this bone disease.
Phosphate rises, active vitamin D falls, PTH rises. Binders are taken with meals. A bedtime-only dose binds nothing.
miss: Treating the low calcium with a huge calcium load and ignoring the phosphate the patient is eating.
diagramAlt: Phosphate binder timing. Swallow with the meal Bedtime-only dosing binds nothing Watch the calcium-phosphate product

source.name: StatPearls. Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD).
source.says: In CKD, reduced kidney function leads to impaired phosphate excretion and decreased synthesis of active vitamin D (calcitriol or 1,25 dihydroxy vitamin D), resulting in hyperphosphatemia and hypocalcemia. Management strategies for CKD-MBD primarily focus on preventing adverse effects associated with secondary hyperparathyroidism.

title: Emphysematous pyelonephritis is gas in a diabetic kidney
lead: Gas in the kidney of a diabetic patient is emphysematous pyelonephritis. It is a surgical and antibiotic emergency, not a routine pyelonephritis.
lines: The organism is often Escherichia coli or another gas-forming gram-negative rod.
A plain film or a CT shows the gas. The urine culture comes later.
Antibiotics alone fail when the gas and the necrosis are established.
Gas in the kidney on CT in a diabetic patient is a necrotizing infection, usually E. coli or another gram-negative rod.
Intravenous antibiotics and drainage or nephrectomy. Oral ciprofloxacin and discharge is the miss.
miss: Sending a diabetic with flank pain and a gas-filled kidney home on an oral antibiotic.

source.name: StatPearls. Emphysematous Pyelonephritis.
source.says: This condition frequently leads to gas formation in the renal parenchyma, collecting system, or perinephric tissue. Individuals with diabetes mellitus are primarily affected by EPN, posing a substantial risk, with reported mortality rates ranging from 40% to 90%. Treatment options for EPN have evolved, with aggressive surgical intervention and more conservative therapeutic approaches, primarily involving percutaneous drainage and antimicrobials.

title: Infantile polycystic kidney disease brings liver fibrosis
lead: Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease presents in infancy and pairs the kidney cysts with congenital hepatic fibrosis.
lines: It is not the adult disease that causes berry aneurysms.
Severe disease causes oligohydramnios and the Potter sequence.
The family pattern is recessive. The parents can be unaffected.
miss: Counseling an infant's family with the adult polycystic-kidney script.

source.name: StatPearls. Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease.
source.says: ARPKD most commonly results from mutations in Polycystic Kidney and Hepatic Disease 1 (PKHD1), leading to renal cysts and congenital hepatic fibrosis in early life.

title: Minimal change disease is nephrotic and foot processes are the lesion
lead: Minimal change disease is nephrotic syndrome, usually in a child, with foot-process effacement and a response to steroids.
lines: The light microscope looks normal. That is the point of the name.
Selective albumin loss is the urine.
A child with sudden edema and heavy protein is this until a steroid trial or a biopsy says otherwise.
Steroids are the first treatment unless hematuria, low complement, or an atypical age demands a biopsy.
miss: Biopsying every edematous child before a specialist has considered the steroid-responsive disease.

source.name: StatPearls. Minimal Change Disease.
source.says: Minimal change disease (MCD) is one of the most common causes of idiopathic nephrotic syndrome in children. Light microscopy of renal biopsy specimens from patients with MCD shows minimal to no change; however, electron microscopy reveals the effacement of podocyte foot processes. Minimal change disease is distinctive for proteinuria that results in edema and intravascular volume depletion, with a good response to steroids.

title: Membranous nephropathy is the adult nephrotic with spikes
lead: Membranous nephropathy is nephrotic syndrome in an adult. The capillary wall thickens, and silver stain shows spikes.
lines: Antibodies to the phospholipase A2 receptor mark the primary disease.
Cancers, hepatitis B, and lupus are the secondary causes to name.
A renal vein thrombosis is the clot this protein loss allows.
miss: Calling every adult nephrotic syndrome minimal change and expecting a quick steroid cure.

source.name: StatPearls. Membranous Nephropathy.
source.says: It is the most common cause of primary nephrotic syndrome in White adults. Silver stain: Spikes (represent staining of basement membrane between the deposits).

title: A malignant effusion is an exudate until cytology says so
lead: A pleural effusion in a patient with cancer or a heavy smoking history is an exudate until the fluid is examined. Cytology is the test that names a malignant effusion.
lines: Heart-failure fluid is a transudate. It is not bloody and not a high protein.
A second sample raises the cytology yield. One negative tap does not clear a suspicious effusion.
Draining the fluid treats the breathlessness. It does not treat the cancer.
miss: Diuresing a bloody, high-protein effusion as if it were heart failure.

source.name: StatPearls. Malignant Pleural Effusion.
source.says: Between 42% and 77% of effusions in cancer patients have been documented to be exudative. Techniques such as pleural fluid cytology, cell block preparation, and pleural biopsy, including image-guided and thoracoscopic biopsies, enhance diagnostic accuracy.

title: Which liver zone dies
lead: Zone 3 is the least oxygenated and the richest in CYP enzymes. Acetaminophen and ischemia necrose zone 3.
lines: Zone 1, around the portal tract, sees the most oxygen. Direct toxins such as phosphorus hit it.
Zone 3 is centrilobular. Chronic passive congestion also injures it and produces the nutmeg liver.
The zone names the mechanism. It does not name every hepatitis.
miss: Putting acetaminophen necrosis in the periportal zone because that zone sees the blood first.

source.name: StatPearls. Acetaminophen Toxicity. Physiology, Liver.
source.says: Zone III has the lowest perfusion due to its distance from the portal triad. At higher doses and as these pathways saturate, CYP oxidation of acetaminophen forms a toxic, oxidative metabolite and depletes hepatic glutathione stores. Hepatocellular centrilobular (zone 3) necrosis.

more.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Liver.

title: Indirect bilirubin or direct
lead: Unconjugated bilirubin is not in the urine. Conjugated bilirubin is.
lines: Hemolysis, Gilbert, and Crigler-Najjar raise unconjugated bilirubin. The liver has not made it water soluble.
Dubin-Johnson, Rotor, hepatitis, and obstruction raise conjugated bilirubin. Dubin-Johnson has a black liver and a defective canalicular exporter.
Jaundice in the first 24 hours of life is not physiologic.
miss: Ordering a urine bilirubin and expecting it to be positive in hemolysis.
diagramAlt: Which bilirubin is in the urine. Unconjugated: not in urine Conjugated: spills into urine First 24 hours of life is not physiologic

source.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Bilirubin.
source.says: Conjugation of bilirubin to the water-soluble form involves the disruption of the hydrogen bonds, an essential process for its elimination by the liver and kidney. Conjugated bilirubin that escapes reuptake into the hepatocyte is excreted in the urine. This inefficient process allows for always having the ability to measure a concentration of unconjugated bilirubin bound to albumin in the venous circulation.

title: Achalasia does not relax the sphincter and does not peristalse
lead: Achalasia fails to relax the lower esophageal sphincter and fails to peristalse. The barium swallow is a bird’s beak.
lines: The patient regurgitates undigested food and can aspirate at night.
Manometry is the confirmatory test.
Cancer at the junction can mimic it. An endoscopy still happens.
Failure of LES relaxation and absent peristalsis. Bird-beak barium. Manometry confirms. Endoscopy excludes a cancer mimic.
Treatment disrupts the sphincter (dilation, myotomy). A proton-pump inhibitor does not. Aspirating patients are kept from eating until that plan is set.
miss: Treating a bird’s beak with a proton-pump inhibitor and no manometry.

source.name: StatPearls. Achalasia.
source.says: Achalasia represents a disorder of esophageal smooth muscle motility in which the lower esophageal sphincter fails to relax, and peristalsis in the esophageal body is absent. Classic findings include smooth tapering of the lower esophagus to a “bird’s beak” appearance, proximal esophageal dilatation, and absent peristalsis during fluoroscopy.

title: Celiac disease flattens the villi
lead: Celiac disease is immune damage to the small-bowel villi from gluten. The blood test is IgA tissue transglutaminase, and IgA deficiency hides it.
lines: Dermatitis herpetiformis is the skin version.
Iron deficiency that will not correct is a clue, because the duodenum is where iron is absorbed.
HLA-DQ2 or DQ8 is necessary and not sufficient. A positive gene test does not diagnose the disease.
Order IgA tissue transglutaminase and a total IgA while the patient is still eating gluten. A gluten-free week before the test can make it falsely negative.
miss: Diagnosing celiac disease from a gene test, or missing it because total IgA was never measured.

source.name: StatPearls. Celiac Disease.
source.says: Exposure to gluten damages the small intestinal mucosa, resulting in villous atrophy, malabsorption, gastrointestinal symptoms, and a wide range of extraintestinal manifestations, including anemia, osteoporosis, and fatigue. When the history and physical examination findings suggest celiac disease, the 2023 American College of Gastroenterology (ACG) guidelines recommend initial serologic testing with tTG-IgA in patients who are not IgA deficient. If IgA deficiency has not been previously assessed, a total IgA level should be measured concurrently.

more.name: ACG Clinical Guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Celiac Disease (2023).

title: Ulcerative colitis starts at the rectum and stays continuous
lead: Ulcerative colitis is continuous mucosal inflammation that starts in the rectum. The stool is bloody.
lines: It does not skip. A skip and a full-thickness bowel is the other inflammatory bowel disease.
Toxic megacolon is dilation, fever, and toxicity. Antidiarrheals make it worse.
A long-standing colitis raises the colon-cancer risk. Surveillance is part of the disease.
miss: Giving an antimotility drug to a toxic, dilated colitis.
diagramAlt: Severe ulcerative colitis. Admit. IV steroid Stop loperamide and opioids C. difficile test. Megacolon: call surgery

source.name: StatPearls. Ulcerative Colitis.
source.says: Typically, the disease starts in the rectum and extends proximally in a continuous manner. The main symptom of ulcerative colitis is bloody diarrhea, with or without mucus.

title: Chronic pancreatitis calcifies and malabsorbs
lead: Chronic pancreatitis hurts, calcifies, and fails: steatorrhea and diabetes from lost exocrine and endocrine tissue.
lines: Alcohol is the common cause. Cystic fibrosis is the young cause.
Enzymes are replaced with food. The pain is a separate problem.
A cancer in the head of the pancreas can obstruct and mimic the pain. Do not assume every calcified pancreas is benign.
Fecal elastase is low. Enzymes are taken with every meal and snack, not at bedtime alone.
Alcohol cessation is the disease-modifying step. New jaundice is imaged as cancer, not treated with more enzymes.
miss: Treating steatorrhea with an antidiarrheal and no enzymes.

source.name: StatPearls. Chronic Pancreatitis.
source.says: Exocrine dysfunction leads to pancreatic insufficiency, steatorrhea, and weight loss, occurring when over 90% of the organ is damaged. Over time, normal pancreatic parenchyma is replaced by fibrotic tissue, causing chronic abdominal pain, malabsorption due to exocrine insufficiency, and diabetes mellitus.

title: Hepatitis B is a DNA virus that uses a reverse transcriptase
lead: Hepatitis B is a DNA virus that replicates through an RNA step. The vaccine antigen is the surface antigen.
lines: Surface antigen means infection now. Surface antibody alone is vaccine or resolved infection.
Core antibody means exposure. The vaccine does not create it.
E antigen marks high infectivity. The virus is DNA but copies through an RNA step.
There is a vaccine. There is not a cure in the hepatitis C sense.
miss: Reading a positive surface antibody as active infection, or missing that the vaccine does not create core antibody.

source.name: StatPearls. Hepatitis B; Hepatitis B Vaccine.
source.says: Antibodies produced by vaccination target the outer protein coat or surface antigen. The current preferred method is a regimen of 3 doses of the recombinant vaccine over 6 months.

more.name: StatPearls. Hepatitis B Vaccine.

title: Hepatitis C is curable and has no vaccine
lead: Hepatitis C is an RNA virus. There is no vaccine. Direct-acting antivirals cure most patients.
lines: Chronic infection is the usual outcome of an untreated acute infection.
Antibody means exposure. Viral RNA means infection now.
Cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma are why the RNA is treated, not watched forever.
There is no vaccine. Cirrhosis still needs hepatocellular-carcinoma surveillance after cure.
miss: Telling a patient with a positive antibody that they are infectious without an RNA, or that there is a vaccine.

source.name: AASLD/IDSA HCV guidance. HCV testing and linkage to care.
source.says: HCV antibody testing with reflex HCV RNA polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing is recommended for initial HCV testing. A positive HCV antibody test indicates current (active) HCV infection (acute or chronic); past infection that has resolved; or a rare false positive.

more.name: StatPearls. Hepatitis C.

title: Wilson disease is a young person with liver disease and a movement problem
lead: Wilson disease cannot excrete copper. Ceruloplasmin is low, the cornea may show a Kayser-Fleischer ring, and the basal ganglia are injured.
lines: The ring needs a slit lamp. Its absence does not exclude liver-only disease.
A chelator or zinc is the treatment. A low-copper diet alone is not.
Basal ganglia injury is the movement disorder. Ceruloplasmin is usually low.
miss: Diagnosing psychiatric disease for a year in a young adult with a tremor and a high bilirubin.

source.name: StatPearls. Wilson Disease.
source.says: Wilson disease is an autosomal recessive condition caused by 1 of several mutations in ATP7B gene which encodes the ATP7B protein transporter on the long arm of chromosome 13 (13q) responsible for excreting excess copper into bile and out of the body. The first serologic test recommended is serum ceruloplasmin, where a level of <20 mg/dL indicates an abnormality. Excess copper then leads to the formation of a toxic hydroxyl group, increasing oxidative stress in the cells and damaging tissue, which can result in organ dysfunction and clinical symptoms, including liver failure, neuropsychiatric symptoms, movement disorders, and Kayser-Fleischer (KF) rings in the cornea.

title: Alpha-1 antitrypsin hits the bases of the lungs and the liver
lead: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency causes basilar emphysema and liver disease. The PAS-positive globules sit in the hepatocyte.
lines: The liver disease is the protein stuck in the cell, not the missing enzyme in the blood alone.
Smoking accelerates the lung injury. Stopping is part of the treatment.
Basal panacinar emphysema, not the apical centrilobular pattern of ordinary smoking. PAS-positive globules in hepatocytes.
Check the level in a young smoker with basal disease. Smoking cessation is the urgent intervention.
miss: Calling basal emphysema ordinary COPD and never checking the level.

source.name: StatPearls. Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency.
source.says: 2 distinct characteristics of AAT-related emphysema are the early onset of symptoms at a young age and a basilar-predominant pattern of emphysema. These inclusions can be detected as positive on periodic acid–Schiff staining with diastase digestion.

title: Primary biliary cholangitis itches and has a mitochondrial antibody
lead: Primary biliary cholangitis is a middle-aged woman with itching, a high alkaline phosphatase, and antimitochondrial antibody.
lines: Xanthelasma comes from the cholesterol the cholestasis raises.
Ursodeoxycholic acid is the disease-modifying drug.
It is not primary sclerosing cholangitis, which is the bile-duct beading of a patient with inflammatory bowel disease.
Itching and xanthelasma come from cholestasis. This is not the beading disease of inflammatory bowel disease.
miss: Chasing a common-duct stone for months in a woman with a positive mitochondrial antibody.

source.name: StatPearls. Primary Biliary Cholangitis.
source.says: Patients may initially be asymptomatic or present with fatigue, pruritus, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies. Asymptomatic patients may be diagnosed after incidental detection of abnormal liver chemistry results, primarily elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and γ-glutamyltransferase levels. AMAs are detected in more than 90% of patients.

title: Sclerosing cholangitis beads the ducts and follows the bowel
lead: Primary sclerosing cholangitis beads the intrahepatic and extrahepatic ducts and travels with inflammatory bowel disease.
lines: The cancer it adds is cholangiocarcinoma. A rising bilirubin is not always a benign stricture.
p-ANCA can be positive. It does not replace the cholangiogram.
Ursodeoxycholic acid is not the proven disease-modifying drug it is in primary biliary cholangitis.
miss: Treating the two cholestatic diseases with the same drug and the same cancer worry.

source.name: StatPearls. Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
source.says: The diagnosis of PSC is primarily based on imaging findings that demonstrate characteristic multifocal strictures of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts with intervening normal or dilated segments, which result in the characteristic “beaded” appearance. A strong association exists with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), particularly ulcerative colitis, which occurs in 60% to 80% of PSC cases.

title: Which adrenal enzyme is blocked
lead: 21-hydroxylase loses cortisol and aldosterone and spills androgens. 11-beta and 17-alpha both cause hypertension and low potassium, and only 17-alpha loses androgens.
lines: 21-hydroxylase is the common block. 17-hydroxyprogesterone is high. The severe form wastes salt.
11-beta-hydroxylase builds deoxycorticosterone, so blood pressure is high and potassium is low, and androgens are still high.
17-alpha-hydroxylase cannot make cortisol or sex steroids. Deoxycorticosterone is high. Genetic males are under-virilized.
miss: Calling every virilized infant 21-hydroxylase, including the one with hypertension.
diagramAlt: Three blocks. 21-hydroxylase: low cortisol, low aldosterone, high androgens. 11-beta-hydroxylase: low cortisol, high deoxycorticosterone, high androgens. 17-alpha-hydroxylase: low cortisol, high deoxycorticosterone, low androgens.

source.name: StatPearls. Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia.
source.says: As a result, 21-OH deficiency hinders the conversion of 17-OHP to 11-deoxycortisol, the penultimate step in cortisol synthesis, and the conversion of progesterone to deoxycorticosterone (DOC) in aldosterone synthesis. Additionally, deficiencies in 11β-OH (CYP11B1/6p21.1) and 17α-OH (CYP17A1/10q24.3) result in the accumulation of mineralocorticoid precursors, causing hypertension and cortisol deficiency in affected individuals. In CAH variants with insufficient sex steroid production, such as StAR, PSCC, 17α-OH, 3β-HSD-2, and possibly POR, sex steroid supplementation may be required at appropriate ages to support normal pubertal development.

title: How the thyroid makes hormone
lead: Thyroid peroxidase organifies iodide and couples the tyrosines. Excess iodide briefly shuts that step off.
lines: The sodium-iodide symporter traps iodide. Perchlorate and thiocyanate block the trap.
Wolff-Chaikoff is the temporary organification block after an iodine load. Jod-Basedow is hyperthyroidism when a nodular gland gets that iodine.
Methimazole and propylthiouracil block thyroid peroxidase. Propylthiouracil also blocks conversion of T4 to T3 outside the gland.
In thyroid storm, a thionamide comes before iodine. Iodine first supplies substrate for more hormone.
miss: Using propylthiouracil and methimazole as if they had the same peripheral effect.

source.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Thyroid Hormone.
source.says: TPO has three functions: oxidation, organification, and coupling reaction.

title: The order of the menstrual cycle
lead: A sustained high estradiol triggers the LH surge. Progesterone rises only after ovulation.
lines: FSH recruits the follicle. Estradiol then restrains FSH until a sustained rise, about 200 pg/mL for about 50 hours, triggers the LH surge.
Ovulation follows that surge. Progesterone rises only afterward, raises the temperature, and thickens cervical mucus.
No hCG, and the corpus luteum fails in about 14 days. Progesterone falls and menses starts.
A progesterone peak drawn before the LH surge is the wrong sequence. Progesterone is the luteal hormone.
miss: Putting the progesterone peak before the LH surge.
diagramAlt: Cycle order. FSH recruits the follicle. Sustained estradiol triggers the LH surge. Ovulation follows. The corpus luteum then makes progesterone.

source.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Menstrual Cycle.
source.says: When a critical level of 17-β estradiol is reached, it provides positive feedback to the anterior pituitary, leading to a surge in FSH and LH production. When ovulation does not occur, no corpus luteum develops, and progesterone is not secreted in significant quantities.

title: Read the calcium and the PTH together
lead: High calcium with a high or unsuppressed PTH is primary hyperparathyroidism. High calcium with a low PTH is PTH-independent.
lines: Primary hyperparathyroidism also lowers the phosphate.
PTHrP from cancer looks the same on the chemistries and the PTH is low.
Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia keeps the urine calcium low. Do not send that patient to parathyroidectomy on the blood calcium alone.
High calcium with a PTH that is high or not suppressed is primary hyperparathyroidism. PTHrP malignancy suppresses PTH.
miss: Removing a parathyroid gland because the calcium is high and the urine calcium was never measured.

source.name: StatPearls. Primary Hyperparathyroidism.
source.says: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is an endocrine disorder defined by autonomous overproduction of parathyroid hormone (PTH), resulting in hypercalcemia and disrupted calcium homeostasis. PTH levels are described as “inappropriately normal” because they do not suppress in response to hypercalcemia.

title: Which Cushing's suppresses
lead: Low-dose dexamethasone fails in every Cushing syndrome. High-dose dexamethasone suppresses a pituitary source and not an adrenal or ectopic one.
lines: The first job is to show that cortisol is high and does not suppress. That does not name the organ.
ACTH is low when the adrenal gland itself is the source. ACTH is high or normal when the source is pituitary or ectopic.
CRH raises ACTH further from a pituitary adenoma and does not raise it from an ectopic source.
miss: Stopping after a failed low-dose test and calling the source pituitary.

source.name: StatPearls. Hypercortisolism (Cushing Syndrome).
source.says: Similarly, a serum ACTH level greater than 20 pg/mL is highly suggestive of ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism, which then brings up the clinical decision branch point of distinguishing between pituitary-based hypercortisolism versus ectopic ACTH syndrome (EAS) through additional dynamic tests (eg, high-dose dexamethasone suppression, CRH stimulation).

title: Thyroid storm: PTU, then iodide an hour later
lead: A Burch-Wartofsky score of 45 or more marks thyroid storm. The order is a beta blocker and propylthiouracil, iodide at least 1 hour later, and a glucocorticoid. Aspirin is not the fever drug.
lines: Propylthiouracil is the thionamide preferred in storm because it also blocks conversion of T4 to T3.
Give iodide at least 1 hour after the thionamide. Iodide first supplies substrate for more hormone.
Add a beta blocker and a glucocorticoid. Cool with acetaminophen, not aspirin.
A score of 45 or more supports the diagnosis. A beta blocker alone is not the regimen.
miss: Giving iodide before the thionamide, or using aspirin for the fever.
diagramAlt: Thyroid storm sequence. PTU first. Iodide at least 1 hour later Beta blocker and a glucocorticoid BWPS >=45. No aspirin

source.name: StatPearls. Thyroid Storm.
source.says: An hour after administering propylthiouracil or methimazole, give SSKI; propylthiouracil is favored because it also blocks peripheral conversion of T4 to T3. Hydrocortisone is started, aspirin is avoided, and a Burch-Wartofsky score of 45 or more is more sensitive for thyroid storm.

more.name: 2016 American Thyroid Association guideline for hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis.

title: Primary adrenal failure is low cortisol and high ACTH
lead: Primary adrenal insufficiency cannot make cortisol or aldosterone. ACTH is high, the skin darkens, and potassium rises.
lines: Crisis dose: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV now, then 200 mg over the next 24 hours, with saline.
Do not wait for a corticotropin stimulation test. Recommendation 4.1 treats the unstable patient first.
After recovery, adult maintenance is hydrocortisone 15 to 25 mg a day in divided doses plus fludrocortisone about 0.1 mg.
Send the patient out with stress-dose teaching and a parenteral glucocorticoid for the next emergency.
miss: Holding the glucocorticoid until a stimulation test is finished in an unstable patient.

source.name: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. Diagnosis and Treatment of Primary Adrenal Insufficiency.
source.says: The signs of PAI are mainly based on the deficiency of gluco- and mineralocorticoids and the resultant weight loss, orthostatic hypotension due to dehydration, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, changes in blood count (anemia, eosinophilia, lymphocytosis), and hypoglycemia. Enhanced secretion of ACTH and other pro-opiomelanocortin peptides often leads to the characteristic hyperpigmentation of the skin and mucous membranes.

title: A functional pheochromocytoma is blocked before surgery
lead: Pheochromocytoma is episodic headache, palpitations, and hypertension. Block alpha receptors before you block beta.
lines: Screen with plasma free metanephrines or urinary fractionated metanephrines. A positive result is followed up, not ignored.
Every patient with a functional tumor gets preoperative blockade before surgery.
Preparation includes a high-sodium diet and a high fluid intake so the blood pressure does not collapse after the tumor is removed.
Block the tumor before incision and load salt and volume so the pressure does not collapse after removal.
miss: Taking a functional pheochromocytoma to surgery without preoperative blockade and volume preparation.

source.name: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma.
source.says: Initial biochemical testing should include plasma free or urinary fractionated metanephrines, and all positive results require follow-up. All patients with functional tumors should undergo preoperative blockade, with a high-sodium diet and fluid intake to prevent postoperative hypotension.

title: Acromegaly is IGF-1, not a random growth-hormone level
lead: Acromegaly is excess growth hormone in an adult. The screening test is IGF-1, because growth hormone pulses.
lines: The jaw, the hands, the sweat, and the glucose intolerance are the picture.
Colon polyps are more common. Screening is part of the disease.
A glucose suppression test confirms when IGF-1 is hard to interpret. Failure to suppress is the abnormal result.
miss: Excluding the disease with one random growth-hormone level.

source.name: StatPearls. Acromegaly.
source.says: The resulting production of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) causes the characteristic overgrowth of certain tissues. IGF-1 is used as it does not vary with sleep patterns, exercise, or throughout the day like GH does.

title: A prolactin is high until pregnancy and drugs are excluded
lead: A high prolactin with amenorrhea and galactorrhea is a prolactinoma only after pregnancy, hypothyroidism, and drugs are excluded.
lines: Antipsychotics and metoclopramide raise prolactin.
A dopamine agonist is the treatment of a prolactinoma, not surgery first.
A very high level, or a headache and a visual-field cut, is a macroadenoma until the MRI says otherwise.
Exclude pregnancy, hypothyroidism, and antipsychotics or metoclopramide before calling it a tumor.
miss: Sending a patient to pituitary surgery before a pregnancy test and a medication review.

source.name: StatPearls. Prolactinoma.
source.says: Evaluation begins with measurement of serum prolactin levels and exclusion of secondary causes, including pregnancy, hypothyroidism, and medication-induced hyperprolactinemia.

title: Endometriosis is endometrium where it should not be
lead: Endometriosis is endometrial tissue outside the uterus. The pain is cyclic, and a chocolate cyst is an endometrioma.
lines: Infertility is part of the disease, not a separate complaint.
The diagnosis that counts is laparoscopy when the story needs it. A normal exam does not exclude it.
Hormonal suppression treats pain. It does not remove a large endometrioma by itself.
miss: Reassuring cyclic pain and infertility because the pelvic exam was normal.

source.name: StatPearls. Endometriosis.
source.says: Ovarian endometrioma, superficial peritoneal endometriosis, and deep infiltrating endometriosis comprise the 3 different endometriosis phenotypes. Laparoscopy may be particularly useful when the diagnosis is uncertain, when patients want definitive confirmation, or if symptoms persist despite empiric therapy. Prevalence is substantially higher, up to 35% to 50%, among patients with chronic pelvic pain or infertility.

title: DKA is insulin deficiency and an anion-gap acid
lead: Diabetic ketoacidosis is no insulin effect, a high anion-gap acidosis, and ketones. Glucose is high, but euglycemic ketoacidosis exists on an SGLT2 inhibitor.
lines: Potassium may look normal while the body is depleted. Insulin will drop the serum potassium.
Fluids first. Insulin after you know the potassium is not critically low.
Resolution, ketones with pH or bicarbonate, matters more than the glucose. Add dextrose when the glucose falls and the ketoacidosis has not resolved.
miss: Stopping insulin when the glucose normalizes while the patient is still acidotic.
diagramAlt: DKA order. Fluid first K under 3.5: replace K before insulin Keep insulin on; add dextrose as glucose falls

source.name: Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report (ADA, EASD, JBDS, AACE, DTS).
source.says: Once plasma glucose is below 250 mg/dL, fluids should contain 5-10% dextrose. With potassium below 3.5 mmol/L, start potassium replacement and delay insulin until potassium is above 3.5 mmol/L. Routine bicarbonate is not recommended. Resolution is ketones <0.6 mmol/L and pH ≥7.3 or bicarbonate ≥18 mmol/L; the anion gap should not be used.

title: Klinefelter is XXY, tall, and infertile
lead: Klinefelter syndrome is 47,XXY. The patient is tall, the testes are small, and sperm production fails.
lines: Gynecomastia and a higher breast-cancer risk are part of the extra X.
Testosterone is low and the gonadotropins are high.
The intelligence is usually normal. Do not confuse it with a cognitive syndrome.
Testosterone treats the hypogonadism. It does not restore sperm. Breast cancer risk is higher than in other men.
Small firm testes, tall stature, azoospermia, and gynecomastia. Testosterone is low and LH and FSH are high.
miss: Diagnosing Marfan syndrome from the height and missing the small testes.

source.name: StatPearls. Klinefelter Syndrome.
source.says: The most common karyotype in Klinefelter syndrome is 47,XXY, accounting for >90%. Levels of the gonadotropins—follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH)—are typically elevated in the setting of testicular hyalinization and fibrosis. Gynecomastia is common, and affected individuals are at an increased risk of developing male breast cancer.

title: Abruption hurts and can consume clotting factors
lead: Placental abruption is painful vaginal bleeding with a uterus that does not relax. The blood can be hidden and the clotting factors consumed.
lines: Hypertension and trauma are the setups.
The fetal heart rate is the monitor that matters while the mother is resuscitated.
Previa is the painless one. A digital exam is the error in previa, not the treatment of abruption.
Placental abruption is painful bleeding and is managed by maternal resuscitation and a prompt delivery decision. Do not perform a digital examination until placenta previa is excluded.
miss: Calling every third-trimester bleed previa and performing a cervical check.

source.name: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 63. Antepartum Haemorrhage.
source.says: If placenta praevia is possible, digital vaginal examination should not be performed until ultrasound has excluded it. With abruption and fetal death, coagulopathy and hypovolaemic shock are not uncommon; in major haemorrhage, send a coagulation screen and cross-match 4 units of blood.

title: Previa is painless, and the finger stays out
lead: In placenta previa the placenta covers the internal cervical os, so the baby cannot pass it and labor is not a safe plan.
lines: Ultrasound makes the diagnosis. The exam that confirms it is speculum only if a clinician who can act is present, and often imaging is enough.
A prior cesarean raises the chance the placenta has grown into the scar.
The delivery is operative when the placenta covers the cervix.
The placenta covers the internal os, so labor and a digital exam can cause hemorrhage. Ultrasound makes the diagnosis.
miss: A digital examination to see how dilated a painlessly bleeding patient is.

source.name: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 27a. Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta Spectrum.
source.says: A placenta is recorded as praevia if it covers the internal os, partially or completely. Placenta praevia carries a high risk of emergency caesarean birth and haemorrhage, so birth is arranged in a unit with blood transfusion and critical care. A previous caesarean with a low-lying placenta or praevia means high risk of placenta accreta spectrum.

title: Glucose crosses the placenta and insulin does not
lead: In gestational diabetes, maternal glucose crosses to the fetus and maternal insulin does not. The fetus makes extra insulin and grows large.
lines: Screening is in the second half of pregnancy, around 24 to 28 weeks if there is no earlier indication.
After birth the baby's insulin is still high and the glucose falls.
The mother's diabetes of pregnancy usually leaves. The risk of later type 2 diabetes stays.
miss: Reassuring a large baby without a glucose test, or forgetting the newborn's hypoglycemia.
diagramAlt: Infant of a diabetic mother. Glucose crosses. Insulin does not Baby is hyperinsulinemic and can be hypoglycemic Feed early. Check a glucose

source.name: StatPearls. Gestational Diabetes.
source.says: Elevated maternal serum glucose levels cross the placenta and produce fetal hyperglycemia, stimulating the fetal pancreas. Insulin does not cross the placental barrier and is recommended by the ADA for first-line treatment of GDM.

title: A PDE-5 inhibitor and a nitrate do not mix
lead: Erection physiology runs on cGMP. A PDE-5 inhibitor preserves it, and a nitrate on top of that drops the pressure.
lines: The contraindication is recent nitrate use, including the nitrate given for chest pain.
Ask before you prescribe, and ask again before you give nitroglycerin.
Psychogenic, vascular, and drug causes of erectile dysfunction are separated by the history, not by the drug.
Sildenafil and a nitrate together can drop systolic pressure profoundly. Ask before the first spray.
If the time of the last dose is unknown, do not give the nitrate. The ECG and aspirin still happen.
miss: Giving nitroglycerin to a patient who took sildenafil this morning.

source.name: StatPearls. Erectile Dysfunction.
source.says: Nitric oxide stimulates the production of cyclic guanosine monophosphate (GMP) when it enters the smooth muscle. PDE-5 inhibitors act by decreasing the degradation of cyclic GMP via phosphodiesterase inhibition, which increases the relaxation of cavernosal smooth muscle and intracavernosal arterial blood flow. They should not be used at all with nitrates due to potentially dangerous, profound hypotension .

title: Prostate growth is DHT and smooth-muscle tone
lead: Benign prostatic hyperplasia obstructs by bulk and by smooth-muscle tone. DHT drives the bulk. Alpha receptors drive the tone.
lines: An alpha blocker works in days and can drop the pressure.
A hard, nodular gland or a high PSA is cancer until evaluated. This disease is smooth and symmetric.
Acute retention is a catheter and a recorded residual. Finasteride does not empty the bladder tonight. A nodule is cancer until evaluated.
miss: Treating a nodular prostate as simple hyperplasia and never examining it.
diagramAlt: BPH drugs. Alpha blocker: days 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor: months, large gland Retention tonight: catheter, not finasteride

source.name: StatPearls. Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
source.says: Testosterone is converted to DHT by 5-alpha-reductase 2 in prostatic stromal cells and accounts for 90% of total intraprostatic androgens. Alpha-blockers are designed to minimize muscle tone in prostate stromal smooth muscle and bladder neck tissue.

title: Testicular torsion has hours, not a clinic slot
lead: Testicular torsion twists the cord. The cremasteric reflex is gone, the pain is sudden, and the testis dies in about six hours.
lines: Do not wait for an ultrasound when the exam is already torsion.
A bell-clapper deformity is the anatomic setup.
The other side is fixed too, because the anatomy is bilateral.
The testis can infarct in about 6 hours. An unclear ultrasound must not use that window up.
miss: Scheduling a Doppler study for the next morning.

source.name: StatPearls. Testicular Torsion.
source.says: The testicle may be swollen, erythematous, and have an absence of the normal cremasteric reflex. Testicular viability significantly decreases 6 hours after the onset of symptoms; hence, early diagnosis is key.

title: Ovarian torsion can have flow and still be twisted
lead: Ovarian torsion is sudden adnexal pain. Doppler flow can still be present, because the ovary has two supplies.
lines: A cyst or a fertility treatment is the setup.
The treatment is surgical detorsion, not a watch-and-wait because flow was seen.
The ovary has a dual blood supply, so Doppler flow can be present in a twisted ovary.
Sudden adnexal pain with a cyst goes to surgery. A pregnancy test is done because ectopic pregnancy is the other emergency.
miss: Reassuring a patient because the Doppler report said flow was present.

source.name: StatPearls. Ovarian Torsion.
source.says: Because the ovary receives a dual blood supply from the ovarian and uterine arteries, arterial or venous flow does not exclude torsion. Pelvic ultrasonography with Doppler flow assessment is the first-line imaging modality recommended for patients with suspected ovarian torsion.

title: Pelvic inflammatory disease reaches the liver capsule
lead: Pelvic inflammatory disease is ascending infection. Cervical motion tenderness is the exam, and perihepatitis is the right-upper-quadrant pain that goes with it.
lines: Treat the patient and the partner.
A tubo-ovarian abscess is the complication that may need drainage.
Ectopic pregnancy is on the differential of pelvic pain until the pregnancy test is negative.
Cervical motion tenderness. Cover Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia. Treat the partner.
Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is perihepatitis and right-upper-quadrant pain.
miss: Treating the cervicitis and not the partner, or missing perihepatitis as cholecystitis.
diagramAlt: PID coverage. Cover gonorrhea and chlamydia Treat the partner Abscess that fails antibiotics: drain

source.name: StatPearls. Pelvic Inflammatory Disease.
source.says: Pelvic inflammatory disease is classically characterized by cervical motion, uterine, and adnexal tenderness on bimanual examination. If the inflammation extends to the liver capsule, patients can develop a perihepatitis, known as Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome, which can cause pleuritic pain in the right upper quadrant that radiates to the right shoulder.

more.name: CDC Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines, 2021. Pelvic inflammatory disease.

title: Postmenopausal bleeding is endometrial cancer until sampled
lead: Bleeding after menopause is endometrial cancer until the endometrium is sampled.
lines: A thin stripe on ultrasound in the right patient lowers the chance. It does not replace a biopsy when the bleeding is real and the risk is high.
Unopposed estrogen is the setup: obesity, tamoxifen, or estrogen without a progestin.
A Pap smear does not sample the endometrium.
miss: Repeating a Pap smear as the workup of postmenopausal bleeding.
diagramAlt: Postmenopausal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy, not a repeat Pap Unopposed estrogen is the setup A thin stripe does not erase persistent bleeding

source.name: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 734. The Role of Transvaginal Ultrasonography in Evaluating the Endometrium of Women With Postmenopausal Bleeding.
source.says: Transvaginal ultrasonography is a reasonable alternative to endometrial sampling as a first approach in an initial episode of bleeding; an endometrial thickness of 4 mm or less has a greater than 99% negative predictive value. If blind sampling does not reveal hyperplasia or malignancy, further testing such as hysteroscopy with D&C is warranted for persistent or recurrent bleeding.

title: Ectopic pregnancy is a positive test and an empty uterus
lead: An ectopic pregnancy is a pregnancy outside the uterus, usually the tube. Pain, bleeding, and a positive test with no intrauterine sac is the picture.
lines: A ruptured ectopic is shock. That patient goes to the operating room.
Methotrexate is for a stable, carefully selected patient. It is not for a patient who is dizzy.
A falling hCG that is still positive needs a plan. It is not a reassurance.
Unstable or ruptured: surgery. Methotrexate only if the patient is stable, the hCG is low, there is no embryonic cardiac activity, and follow-up is certain.
miss: Sending a stable-looking patient home with a positive test and an empty uterus and no follow-up.
diagramAlt: Ectopic pregnancy. Shock or rupture: operating room Methotrexate only if stable and follow-up is sure Rh-negative: give anti-D

source.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 193. Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy (reaffirmed 2025).
source.says: Most tubal ectopic pregnancies detected early can be treated with minimally invasive surgery or with methotrexate. A tubal ectopic pregnancy in an unstable patient is a medical emergency that requires prompt surgical intervention.

title: In pregnancy, PTU covers the first trimester
lead: Propylthiouracil is the antithyroid drug for the first trimester. A woman on methimazole switches to propylthiouracil before conception or as soon as pregnancy is confirmed. After the first trimester, propylthiouracil or methimazole can be used.
lines: Methimazole in early pregnancy carries the larger risk of severe birth defects, so the first trimester belongs to propylthiouracil.
A woman on methimazole switches before conception or on a positive pregnancy test when a drug is still required.
After the first trimester there is no mandatory switch. Continuing propylthiouracil or changing to methimazole are both acceptable.
miss: Continuing methimazole into the first trimester, or treating a later change back to methimazole as mandatory.
diagramAlt: Antithyroid drug in pregnancy. Before conception or on a positive test: switch methimazole to propylthiouracil. First trimester: propylthiouracil. After that: propylthiouracil or methimazole. No radioactive iodine in pregnancy.

source.name: 2017 Guidelines of the American Thyroid Association for the Diagnosis and Management of Thyroid Disease During Pregnancy and the Postpartum.
source.says: If ATD therapy is needed during the first trimester, PTU is preferred over MMI because the risk for severe birth defects is lower. Pregnant women receiving MMI who are in need of continuing therapy during pregnancy should be switched to PTU as early as possible. If ATD therapy is required after 16 weeks gestation, it remains unclear whether PTU should be continued or therapy changed to MMI.

more.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 223. Thyroid Disease in Pregnancy (2020, reaffirmed 2023).
American Thyroid Association 2026 Guidelines for Thyroid Disease in Preconception, Pregnancy, and Postpartum (recommendation text not retrievable here).

title: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause is tissue, not an infection
lead: After menopause, low estrogen thins the vulva and the vagina. Dryness, pain with sex, and urinary urgency are that syndrome until an infection is proved.
lines: A culture comes before repeated antibiotics.
It is not lichen sclerosus, which scars and needs a different exam.
Vaginal estrogen treats local symptoms. Do not prescribe months of antibiotics for a negative culture.
miss: Prescribing antibiotics for months of urgency without an exam or a culture.

source.name: StatPearls. Genitourinary Syndrome of Menopause.
source.says: Menopause causes a dramatic 95% reduction in estrogen production, resulting in 75% of women experiencing vaginal dryness, 40% reporting pain during intercourse, and 30% to 40% experiencing urinary urgency and frequency. GSM encompasses vulvovaginal atrophy, urogenital atrophy, and atrophic vaginitis, involving the vagina, labia, urethra, and bladder as a consequence of diminished estrogenic stimulation.

title: High-risk HPV, not a single Pap, drives cervical cancer
lead: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus, especially types 16 and 18, causes cervical cancer. The Pap and the HPV test find the precancer.
lines: The vaccine is given before exposure to work best.
A single normal Pap does not end screening on the schedule the guidelines set.
Bleeding after sex still gets an exam. A normal recent test does not cancel a symptomatic cervix.
Types 16 and 18 cause most cervical cancers. Screening starts at 21, not at coitarche.
Ages 21–29: cytology every 3 years, not HPV testing alone. Ages 30–65: cytology every 3 years, HPV every 5, or cotesting every 5. Stop at 65 only if prior tests were adequate.
miss: Telling a vaccinated patient she never needs a cervix exam again.
diagramAlt: Cervical screening intervals. Start at 21, not at first sex 21–29: cytology every 3 years 30–65: cytology q3, HPV q5, or both q5

source.name: StatPearls. Cervical Cancer.
source.says: Persistent HPV infection causes more than 99% of all cervical cancers. More than 75% of cervical cancer cases are due to high-risk HPV types 16 and 18.

more.name: USPSTF. Cervical Cancer: Screening (2018).

title: A high TSH can enlarge the pituitary
lead: Severe primary hypothyroidism raises TRH. TRH can raise prolactin and enlarge the pituitary. That enlargement is hyperplasia, not an automatic adenoma to remove.
lines: Treat the thyroid and reimage. The mass can shrink.
A prolactin that is only modestly high with a huge mass is a stalk effect, not a prolactinoma.
Surgery for a pituitary that is hyperplasia from hypothyroidism is the miss.
Replace levothyroxine and reimage before any surgical date.
miss: Sending a patient with a TSH of 80 and a pituitary mass straight to surgery.

source.name: StatPearls. Pituitary Hyperplasia in Primary Hypothyroidism.
source.says: As a result of thyroid destruction, low circulating thyroid hormone levels lead to reduced negative feedback on the hypothalamus, thereby elevating thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH). Elevated TRH levels can also lead to lactotroph hyperplasia, which accounts for the increased prolactin in these patients. Another reason for follow-up imaging is that if there is no regression in the size of the pituitary with the treatment of the underlying hypothyroidism, the clinician should reconsider this diagnosis.

title: The three shock profiles
lead: Hypovolemic and cardiogenic shock both raise systemic vascular resistance and drop cardiac output. Only cardiogenic shock raises the wedge pressure.
lines: Distributive shock drops the resistance. Early on, the cardiac output is high.
Obstruction is not one number. Tamponade equalizes diastolic pressures. A large pulmonary embolus raises right-sided pressure and drops the wedge.
Cold skin fits a high-resistance shock. Warm skin fits a distributive shock.
Hypovolemic: output down, SVR up, wedge down. Cardiogenic: output down, SVR up, wedge up.
miss: Calling every low-output shock hypovolemia and pouring fluid into cardiogenic pulmonary edema.
diagramAlt: Shock table. Hypovolemic: cardiac output down, resistance up, wedge down. Cardiogenic: cardiac output down, resistance up, wedge up. Distributive: cardiac output up, resistance down, wedge down or normal.

source.name: StatPearls. Hypovolemia and Hypovolemic Shock. Cardiogenic Shock. Distributive Shock.
source.says: Hypovolemic : Decreased PCWP, decreased CO, increased SVR. Distributive : Decreased PCWP, increased CO, decreased SVR. Cardiogenic : Increased PCWP, decreased CO, increased SVR.

more.name: StatPearls. Cardiogenic Shock.
StatPearls. Distributive Shock.

title: The gram-positive branch points
lead: Catalase splits staph from strep. Coagulase splits Staphylococcus aureus from the other staphylococci.
lines: Alpha-hemolytic: Streptococcus pneumoniae is optochin sensitive and bile soluble. Viridans streptococci are not.
Beta-hemolytic: group A is bacitracin sensitive. Group B is not. Enterococcus grows in 6.5% salt. Streptococcus gallolyticus does not, and it points at a colon lesion.
Catalase positive: staphylococcus. Coagulase positive: S. aureus. Novobiocin separates saprophyticus (resistant) from epidermidis (sensitive).
Catalase negative: streptococcus. Optochin-sensitive alpha hemolysis is pneumococcus. Bacitracin-sensitive beta hemolysis is group A.
miss: Stopping at gram-positive cocci in clusters and treating a contaminant and an aureus infection as the same organism.
diagramAlt: Branch points. Catalase positive is staphylococcus. Coagulase positive is Staphylococcus aureus. Catalase negative is streptococcus, then split by hemolysis.

source.name: StatPearls. Gram-Positive Bacteria.
source.says: Gram-positive cocci include Staphylococcus (catalase-positive), which forms clusters, and Streptococcus (catalase-negative), which forms chains. The staphylococci are further subdivided into coagulase-positive (S. aureus) and coagulase-negative (S epidermidis and S saprophyticus) species.

title: Which HIV drug blocks which step
lead: NRTIs and NNRTIs block reverse transcriptase. Integrase inhibitors block insertion. Protease inhibitors block maturation.
lines: Entry blockers are separate: CCR5 blockade, fusion blockade, and post-attachment blockade.
A preferred initial regimen is an integrase inhibitor plus two nucleoside analogs, including when the CD4 count is low.
Two drugs that use the same nucleoside pathway, such as two thymidine analogs, are not a pair.
miss: Naming the class without naming the viral step it stops.

source.name: StatPearls. HIV Antiretroviral Therapy.
source.says: Integrase inhibitors block integrase activity, preventing the viral genome from integrating into the host cell's DNA. PIs bind the HIV-1 protease and block the proteolytic cleavage of protein precursors required for viral particle production.

title: Carbon monoxide occupies hemoglobin and shifts the curve left
lead: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin far more tightly than oxygen. PaO2 stays normal, the oxygen content falls, and the curve shifts left.
lines: The pulse oximeter cannot tell carbon monoxide from oxygen.
Cherry-red skin is unreliable. A headache in a family who share a heater is the clue.
Hyperbaric oxygen for coma, pregnancy, ischemia, or a very high level. Check everyone who shared the heater.
miss: Reassuring a normal PaO2 in a patient pulled from a fire.
diagramAlt: Carbon monoxide. PaO2 and pulse ox can look normal Content is low. Curve shifts left 100% oxygen now. Whole household

source.name: StatPearls. Carbon Monoxide Poisoning.
source.says: Carbon monoxide poisoning occurs when the gas binds hemoglobin with an affinity approximately 200 to 250 times greater than oxygen, forming a dysfunctional hemoglobin species that reduces oxygen-carrying capacity and impairs tissue oxygen unloading. This process reduces blood oxygen-carrying capacity and induces a leftward shift of the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve, impairing oxygen release to tissues. Standard pulse oximetry cannot differentiate oxyhemoglobin from COHb, often producing falsely reassuring readings.

title: Acetaminophen injury is NAPQI, and NAC is the antidote
lead: Acetaminophen's toxic metabolite is NAPQI. N-acetylcysteine restores glutathione and is the antidote.
lines: On the treatment line, 150 micrograms per mL at 4 hours is the level that starts acetylcysteine.
Give acetylcysteine within 8 hours of a single acute ingestion when that line is crossed.
The 2023 consensus uses a revised Rumack-Matthew nomogram for a presentation from 4 to 24 hours. A 2-hour level does not clear the patient.
A normal early ALT is not a reason to withhold the antidote.
miss: Waiting past 8 hours, or trusting a 2-hour level, before starting acetylcysteine.
diagramAlt: Acetaminophen antidote. NAPQI uses up glutathione NAC if level is toxic or time is unknown Normal ALT at 2 hours does not clear it

source.name: StatPearls. Acetaminophen Toxicity.
source.says: At therapeutic doses, approximately 8% of acetaminophen is metabolized by hepatic cytochrome P450 subfamilies—particularly CYP2E1—through the mixed-function oxidase pathway, generating a toxic, highly reactive, electrophilic intermediate N-acetyl-p-benzoquinoneimine (NAPQI). At higher doses and as these pathways saturate, CYP oxidation of acetaminophen forms a toxic, oxidative metabolite and depletes hepatic glutathione stores. Acetylcysteine, most often given IV, is the critical antidote for acetaminophen poisoning, and is most effective if administered within the first 8 hours after an acute overdose.

more.name: Management of Acetaminophen Poisoning in the US and Canada: A Consensus Statement (2023).

title: Opioid toxicity is a small pupil and a breath that stops
lead: Opioid toxicity is miosis, respiratory depression, and a depressed mental state. Naloxone reverses the opioid, not the benzodiazepine.
lines: Support ventilation first if the patient is not breathing. Naloxone does not replace that.
Intravenous naloxone in the AHA poisoning guidance is 0.2 to 2 mg. FDA-labeled nasal spray is 4 mg. Repeat every 2 to 3 minutes.
Titrate to breathing and airway reflexes. A long-acting opioid needs a longer watch because depression returns.
A benzodiazepine taken with the opioid does not delay the naloxone.
