miss: One dose of naloxone and a discharge as soon as the patient wakes.
diagramAlt: Naloxone wears off. Opioid half-life is often longer Observe or infuse Methadone and fentanyl outlast one dose

source.name: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and ECC. Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation.
source.says: An opioid antagonist such as naloxone should be given to people with respiratory arrest from suspected opioid overdose. In cardiac arrest from presumed opioid overdose, an opioid antagonist may be reasonable if high-quality CPR is not interrupted.

title: Flumazenil can seize a dependent patient
lead: Benzodiazepine sedation alone rarely stops breathing the way an opioid does. Flumazenil reverses it and can precipitate a seizure if the patient is dependent.
lines: Isolated benzodiazepine poisoning rarely causes life-threatening hypoventilation. Flumazenil is not routine: it can precipitate seizures in a dependent patient, and naloxone has the better safety profile when an opioid may be present.
Do not give flumazenil to a daily user or in a mixed overdose. It can precipitate a seizure.
If an opioid may be on board, give naloxone. The 2023 update treats naloxone as the safer reversal.
Support the airway while you sort out the mix.
miss: Waking a daily benzodiazepine user with flumazenil and causing a seizure.

source.name: StatPearls. Benzodiazepine Toxicity.
source.says: Flumazenil can precipitate acute withdrawal in those with chronic benzodiazepine dependence; given to a dependent patient it can lower the seizure threshold and cause life-threatening seizures.

more.name: 2023 AHA focused update on cardiac arrest or life-threatening toxicity due to poisoning.

title: Delirium tremens is the late alcohol withdrawal
lead: Alcohol withdrawal tremor starts within a day. Seizures follow. Delirium tremens is the confused, unstable state that peaks around two to three days.
lines: A benzodiazepine is the treatment, titrated to the symptoms.
A normal saline bag is not the treatment of the seizure.
Other withdrawal, including benzodiazepine withdrawal, looks similar. The history decides.
Tremor at about 6–24 hours, seizures at 12–48 hours, delirium tremens at 48–72 hours. Use a symptom-triggered benzodiazepine.
Thiamine before any glucose. An antipsychotic alone does not prevent the seizure. Do not discharge a patient still scoring in the severe range.
miss: Treating alcohol-withdrawal delirium with an antipsychotic alone.
diagramAlt: Alcohol withdrawal orders. Thiamine before glucose Benzodiazepine titrated to symptoms Haloperidol alone does not stop the seizure

source.name: The ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management.
source.says: Symptom-triggered treatment by trained staff is the preferred benzodiazepine dosing method with continuous monitoring, and front loading is recommended for patients at high risk of severe withdrawal. Thiamine should be provided to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy, and antipsychotics are not recommended as monotherapy.

title: Rhabdomyolysis dips blood on the stick and has no red cells
lead: Rhabdomyolysis leaks myoglobin. The urine dip is positive for blood and the microscope shows no red cells. The creatine kinase is in the thousands.
lines: A crush, a lying-down overdose, a statin plus a fibrate, and a seizure are the setups.
Fluids protect the kidney. The potassium can kill before the kidney fails.
Compartment syndrome can be the cause and the result. Check the limb.
Dipstick positive for blood and no red cells on microscopy. Potassium can arrest the heart before creatinine rises.
miss: Diagnosing hematuria from a positive dipstick and never looking at the microscope or the CK.
diagramAlt: Rhabdomyolysis labs. Dipstick blood, no RBCs on microscope CK in the thousands. K can kill first IV fluid. Open a tight compartment

source.name: StatPearls. Rhabdomyolysis.
source.says: However, the peroxidase agent used on a urine dipstick to detect blood with also react with myoglobin. Microscopic urinalysis differentiates myoglobinuria from hemoglobinuria, as myoglobinuria is associated with an absence of red blood cells.

title: Malignant hyperthermia is rigidity, CO2, and dantrolene
lead: Malignant hyperthermia is a genetic ryanodine-receptor crisis set off by succinylcholine or a volatile anesthetic. The CO2 rises, the muscle is rigid, and dantrolene is the drug.
lines: Stop the triggering anesthetic.
Cool the patient and treat the potassium.
It is not neuroleptic malignant syndrome, which is a dopamine-blocker disease outside the operating room.
This is not neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
miss: Treating intraoperative rigidity and a rising CO2 as ordinary light anesthesia.
diagramAlt: Malignant hyperthermia. Volatile agent or succinylcholine Rising CO2, then heat and rigidity Stop the gas. Dantrolene. 100% oxygen

source.name: European Malignant Hyperthermia Group. Recognising and managing a malignant hyperthermia crisis (v2024).
source.says: Stop all trigger agents, hyperventilate with 100% oxygen at high flow, and call for help. Give dantrolene 2-2.5 mg/kg IV, repeated every 10 minutes. Inappropriately elevated CO2 production is an early sign, and trigger agents are volatile anaesthetics and succinylcholine.

more.name: EMHG 2024 guideline, Br J Anaesth 2025;134:221-223.

title: Fat embolism follows a long-bone fracture by a day or two
lead: Fat embolism is hypoxia, a petechial rash, and confusion one to three days after a long-bone or pelvic fracture.
lines: The rash is the upper body. It is not present in every patient.
Support the lungs. There is no drug that dissolves the embolus as the first move.
It is not a thrombus that heparin is aimed at, though the patient may have that risk too.
miss: Diagnosing a pulmonary embolus of clot and anticoagulating as the only plan for a petechial, hypoxic fracture patient.

source.name: StatPearls. Fat Embolism and Fat Embolism Syndrome.
source.says: Fat embolism typically manifests 24 to 72 hours after the initial insult, with an average onset time of 48 hours. Trauma-related FES may result from fractures of long bones, including the femur and tibia, and from pelvic fractures. Dermatologic examination : A petechial rash in a patient with the preceding risk factors should raise concern for FES.

title: A septic joint is tapped before the antibiotic if the patient can wait
lead: Septic arthritis is a hot joint that is tapped before antibiotics when the patient is stable. Staph aureus is the organism to name.
lines: The fluid is pus: a high white count and a culture.
A prosthetic joint and gonorrhea are the two stories that change the organism list.
Antibiotics without a culture, in a stable patient, burn the diagnosis.
miss: Starting vancomycin and never aspirating a native knee that could have been tapped.

source.name: StatPearls. Septic Arthritis.
source.says: The evaluation of suspected septic arthritis includes arthrocentesis with synovial fluid analysis, laboratory and imaging studies. Staphylococcus aureus is the most common infecting organism in adults.

more.name: BSR/BHPR, BOA, RCGP and BSAC guideline for the hot swollen joint in adults (2006).

title: Open fractures are contaminated the moment the bone meets the air
lead: An open fracture is a contaminated bone. Antibiotics and tetanus start immediately, and the wound is washed in the operating room.
lines: The clock is hours, not the next clinic day.
A bigger, dirtier wound needs broader antibiotics.
Closing a dirty wound in the emergency department is the miss.
A larger, dirtier wound needs broader coverage. Photograph and document pulses before the dressing hides them.
miss: Splinting an open fracture and arranging antibiotics for the morning.

source.name: StatPearls. Open Fracture Management.
source.says: Antibiotics should be administered as soon as possible in the prehospital setting or emergency department. If a patient has not completed the tetanus series or has not had a booster in the last five years, tetanus toxoid should be given.

title: HIT is an antibody that clots, five to ten days in
lead: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is an antibody to platelet factor 4. Platelets fall 5 to 10 days after heparin, and the clots are the danger.
lines: Estimate probability with the 4Ts score, not a gestalt impression.
A low-probability 4Ts score is not an indication to stop heparin and start another anticoagulant.
An intermediate or high score: stop heparin and start a non-heparin anticoagulant. ASH names argatroban, bivalirudin, danaparoid, fondaparinux, and a direct oral anticoagulant.
Do not start warfarin before the platelet count recovers, usually to at least 150 × 10^9/L. Early warfarin is linked to venous limb gangrene.
miss: Stopping heparin without a non-heparin anticoagulant when the 4Ts score is intermediate or high, or starting warfarin while the platelet count is still low.
diagramAlt: HIT, day 5 to 10. Platelets fall >=50% at day 5-10 With or without thrombosis Stop heparin. No warfarin before recovery

source.name: ASH 2018 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
source.says: Strong recommendations include use of the 4Ts score rather than a gestalt approach and avoidance of empiric treatment of HIT with a low-probability 4Ts score. The panel suggests argatroban, bivalirudin, danaparoid, fondaparinux, or a DOAC, and recommends against a VKA before platelet count recovery (usually ≥150 × 10^9/L).

title: Community pneumonia's severity is the bed, not the bug
lead: The first pneumonia decision is where the patient is treated. Hypoxia, low pressure, and confusion are reasons to stay, not reasons to add an anaerobic drug.
lines: A healthy outpatient is amoxicillin or doxycycline.
A macrolide alone is only where pneumococcal resistance is low.
Routine anaerobic coverage for aspiration is not the guideline.
Hypoxia, hypotension, or confusion is admission. Severe disease is combination therapy, not an oral macrolide.
Do not add anaerobic coverage because the note says aspiration. Blood cultures are for severe disease.
miss: Adding metronidazole because the word aspiration was written in the note.
diagramAlt: Pneumonia: where and which drug. Hypoxia, shock, or confusion: admit Severe: beta-lactam + macrolide No routine anaerobic drug for aspiration

source.name: 2019 ATS/IDSA Guideline for Diagnosis and Treatment of Adults with Community-acquired Pneumonia.
source.says: Combination therapy with a beta-lactam plus a macrolide or a beta-lactam plus a respiratory fluoroquinolone should be the treatment of choice for severe CAP.

title: Long-bone fat and a line infection are different emboli
lead: A fever and a new murmur after a dental procedure or a line is endocarditis. Petechiae after a femur fracture are fat. The timing separates them.
lines: Endocarditis is days of fever and positive blood cultures.
Fat embolism is one to three days after the fracture, with hypoxia.
A single antibiotic does not cover both decisions.
miss: Anticoagulating fat embolism and culturing a fracture patient as if the bone were a valve.

source.name: StatPearls. Fat Embolism and Fat Embolism Syndrome.
source.says: Fat embolism typically manifests 24 to 72 hours after the initial insult, with an average onset time of 48 hours. Trauma-related FES may result from fractures of long bones, including the femur and tibia, and from pelvic fractures.

more.name: StatPearls. Infective Endocarditis.

title: A ring-enhancing brain lesion is not the first lumbar puncture
lead: Fever and a focal brain sign get imaged before a lumbar puncture. A ring can be an abscess, and a needle below it can herniate the brain.
lines: Blood cultures can be drawn while the scanner is called.
Antibiotics for meningitis are not delayed for the scan if the patient is sick. The puncture waits.
Steroids for suspected pneumococcal meningitis go in with the first antibiotic dose.
miss: Puncturing the back of a patient with a blown pupil.

source.name: StatPearls. Brain Abscess.
source.says: Lumbar puncture : Rarely required, a lumbar puncture should only be performed after obtaining a head computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to rule out increased intracranial pressure due to significant mass effect, which can lead to cerebral herniation.

title: Tryptase supports anaphylaxis and does not treat it
lead: Anaphylaxis is IgE on mast cells. A tryptase drawn in the first few hours supports the diagnosis later. It is not the treatment.
lines: Epinephrine is 0.01 mg/kg, to a maximum of 0.3 mg in children and teenagers and 0.5 mg in adults.
Give epinephrine at the first sign of suspected anaphylaxis.
Draw an acute tryptase as early as possible, ideally within 2 hours of symptom onset. A later baseline is the comparison.
A tryptase under the laboratory cutoff does not exclude anaphylaxis. Many confirmed reactions never cross that line.
miss: Treating anaphylaxis with an antihistamine and quoting a flat 0.3 mg dose for every adult.
diagramAlt: Anaphylaxis dose. Adult: 0.3–0.5 mg of 1 mg/mL IM Mid-outer thigh. Repeat in 5–15 min Watch. Antihistamine is not the treatment

source.name: World Allergy Organization Anaphylaxis Guidance 2020.
source.says: During acute anaphylaxis, serum tryptase levels are increased from 15 min to 3 h or even longer, after the onset; levels peak between 1 and 2 h after the onset. Although elevated levels support a diagnosis of anaphylaxis, normal levels do not exclude anaphylaxis having occurred.

more.name: Anaphylaxis: a 2023 practice parameter update.

title: Prevalence moves the predictive value, not the sensitivity
lead: Sensitivity and specificity stay put when the disease gets rarer. The positive predictive value falls.
lines: Sensitivity is true positives over everyone who has the disease. Specificity is true negatives over everyone who does not.
Positive predictive value is true positives over every positive test. It falls as false positives crowd out the true ones.
A screening test in a rare disease can be very sensitive and still be wrong most of the times it says yes.
miss: Quoting sensitivity as if it were the chance the patient has the disease.
diagramAlt: Two-by-two table. Sensitivity reads down the disease column. Specificity reads down the no-disease column. Positive predictive value reads across the positive-test row.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Disease prevalence in a population affects PPV and NPV. Unlike predictive values, and like sensitivity and specificity, likelihood ratios are not affected by disease prevalence.

title: A likelihood ratio moves the odds
lead: Post-test odds equal pre-test odds times the likelihood ratio. A ratio of 1 changes nothing.
lines: The positive likelihood ratio is sensitivity divided by the false-positive rate.
A negative likelihood ratio is 1 minus sensitivity, divided by specificity. A very small one is what rules a disease out.
Do the multiplication in odds, not in probabilities.
miss: Subtracting a likelihood ratio from a probability.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Positive Likelihood Ratio=Sensitivity/(1-Specificity) Negative Likelihood Ratio=(1- Sensitivity)/Specificity.

title: A sensitive test helps when it is negative
lead: A very sensitive test, when negative, lowers the chance of disease. That only helps if you started with a real pre-test chance.
lines: A negative result helps only when sensitivity is high and the pre-test chance was real. That is SnNOut.
False positives come from imperfect specificity, which is 1 minus specificity. Sensitivity does not create them.
Low prevalence amplifies those false positives, so the positive predictive value falls.
miss: Blaming false positives on sensitivity, or treating a negative test as certainty when the pre-test chance was never real.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Highly sensitive tests yield positive results in patients with the disease, whereas highly specific tests show that patients without a positive result do not have the disease.

title: A specific test helps when it is positive
lead: A very specific test, when positive, raises the chance of disease. A positive result in a rare disease can still be wrong.
lines: False positives are what a nonspecific test creates.
SpPIn fails when the positive likelihood ratio is only modest.
Specificity is true negatives over people without the disease. A positive result helps only when that number is high.
miss: Telling a patient a positive nonspecific screening test is the diagnosis.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Highly sensitive tests yield positive results in patients with the disease, whereas highly specific tests show that patients without a positive result do not have the disease. False positives are a consideration when evaluating specificity and PPV.

title: Negative predictive value falls as the disease gets common
lead: As prevalence rises, the negative predictive value falls and the positive predictive value rises. Sensitivity does not move.
lines: Do the math in the population you are standing in.
Predictive values are not printed on the kit as constants.
As prevalence rises, NPV falls and PPV rises. A test that reassured in a screening fair reassures less in an outbreak.
miss: Using the same predictive value in the emergency department and in a screening fair.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Disease prevalence in a population affects PPV and NPV. Unlike predictive values, and like sensitivity and specificity, likelihood ratios are not affected by disease prevalence. When a disease is highly prevalent, the test is better at ‘ruling in' the disease and worse at ‘ruling it out.’.

title: A likelihood ratio of 1 is a test that did nothing
lead: Multiply pre-test odds by the likelihood ratio. A ratio of 1 leaves the odds where they were.
lines: Do this in odds, then convert back to a probability if you need one.
A huge positive ratio is useful. A ratio of 2 barely moves a common disease.
The ratio comes from sensitivity and specificity, so it does not depend on prevalence.
miss: Subtracting the likelihood ratio from the probability.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Positive Likelihood Ratio=Sensitivity/(1-Specificity) Negative Likelihood Ratio=(1- Sensitivity)/Specificity.

title: Moving a cutoff trades sensitivity for specificity
lead: Lower the cutoff of a continuous test and sensitivity rises. Specificity falls, because more healthy people cross the line.
lines: There is no cutoff that maximizes both.
The right cutoff depends on whether a miss or a false alarm hurts more.
A published cutoff from another lab is not automatically yours.
miss: Demanding a test that is both perfectly sensitive and perfectly specific at one number.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Sensitivity and specificity are inversely related: as sensitivity increases, specificity tends to decrease , and vice versa.

title: The false-positive rate is one minus specificity
lead: The false-positive rate is 1 minus specificity. It is the share of well people the test calls sick.
lines: It is not 1 minus the positive predictive value.
A specificity of 95% means 5 of 100 well people are called positive.
A sensitive test can still produce many false positives when specificity is only fair.
miss: Subtracting the positive predictive value from 1 and calling that the false-positive rate.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Specificity=(True Negatives (D))/(True Negatives (D)+False Positives (B)). False positives are a consideration when evaluating specificity and PPV.

title: Either-positive testing catches more and alarms more
lead: If either of two tests being positive counts, sensitivity rises and specificity falls. You miss less and you alarm more.
lines: This is parallel testing.
Series testing does the opposite: both must be positive.
Pick the structure from the cost of a miss versus the cost of a false alarm.
Order the downstream plan for the extra false positives before you order the pair.
miss: Running two tests and treating every positive as if specificity had improved.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Sensitivity and specificity are inversely related: as sensitivity increases, specificity tends to decrease , and vice versa.

title: The negative likelihood ratio uses the misses
lead: The negative likelihood ratio is 1 minus sensitivity, divided by specificity. A very small one is what lets a negative test rule disease out.
lines: If sensitivity is 80%, then 1 minus sensitivity is 0.2, and the negative likelihood ratio stays sizable.
The positive ratio uses the false positives in the denominator.
Neither ratio contains the prevalence.
miss: Using a moderately sensitive test to exclude a dangerous disease.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Negative Likelihood Ratio=(1- Sensitivity)/Specificity. A negative likelihood ratio is “the probability of a patient testing negative who has a disease divided by the probability of a patient testing negative who does not have a disease.”

title: Pre-test probability is decided before the test comes back
lead: The pre-test probability is what you believed before this result. The test revises it. It does not replace it.
lines: A positive test in a patient who almost could not have the disease is still often a false positive.
Write the probability down, even roughly, before you look.
Write the chance before you look at the result. The likelihood ratio revises that number. It does not create it.
A positive test when the pre-test chance is near zero is usually false.
miss: Letting the lab result be the entire diagnosis.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: To make clinical decisions and guide patient care, providers must understand the likelihood that a patient has a disease, integrating pretest probability with diagnostic test results.

title: A signature is not consent
lead: Informed consent is disclosure, understanding, and a voluntary choice. The form is only the record.
lines: Disclosure covers the decision, the alternatives, and the risks a reasonable person would want.
Understanding is checked by asking the patient to say it back, not by watching them sign.
A choice made under pressure, or by someone who cannot decide this question, is not consent.
Informed consent requires disclosure a reasonable patient would want, the patient's understanding, and a voluntary decision. The clinician performing the procedure is responsible for that disclosure.
Use a professional interpreter. A child is not the interpreter. The clinician who performs the procedure obtains the consent.
miss: Treating a signed form as proof the patient understood.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 2.1.1, Informed Consent.
source.says: Assess the patient’s ability to understand relevant medical information and the implications of treatment alternatives and to make an independent, voluntary decision. Document the informed consent conversation and the patient’s (or surrogate’s) decision in the medical record in some manner.

title: When confidentiality yields
lead: Confidentiality yields for a serious imminent threat, and the disclosure is limited to what that threat requires.
lines: The ordinary rule is that the patient's information stays with the team caring for the patient.
A required warning is not a license to brief the family, the employer, or a hallway.
Tell the patient what you must disclose, unless telling them would itself cause the harm.
miss: Either keeping a specific credible threat secret, or announcing it to everyone who asks.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 3.2.1, Confidentiality.
source.says: Restrict disclosure to the minimum necessary information. To other third parties situated to mitigate the threat when in the physician’s judgment there is a reasonable probability that: the patient will seriously harm themself; the patient will inflict serious physical harm on an identifiable individual or individuals.

title: Autonomy is the patient's decision, not the team's preference
lead: Respect for autonomy means a capable patient decides. Beneficence does not outrank a refusal you dislike.
lines: A capable patient's refusal stands even when the team believes the operation is better.
Capacity is four abilities for this decision today: understand, appreciate, reason, and express a choice. It can change when sodium, oxygen, or a sedative changes.
Beneficence does not erase that refusal. Disagreement with the recommendation is not incapacity.
The other principles, nonmaleficence and justice, do not authorize overriding a capable no.
miss: Overriding a capable refusal because the operation is clearly better.
diagramAlt: Capacity for this decision. Understand the facts Appreciate what they mean for you Reason, and say a stable choice

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 1.1.3, Patient Rights.
source.says: A patient who has decision-making capacity may accept or refuse any recommended medical intervention.

title: Truth-telling is the default
lead: You tell the patient the diagnosis. A family request to hide it does not override a patient who wants to know.
lines: Hiding a result to keep the visit short fails the duty.
A therapeutic privilege to withhold is rare and is not a convenience.
Ask how much the patient wants to know and whom to include before you speak to the family.
miss: Telling only the family because they asked you not to upset the patient.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 2.1.3, Withholding Information from Patients.
source.says: Except in emergency situations in which a patient is incapable of making an informed decision, withholding information without the patient’s knowledge or consent is ethically unacceptable.

title: A written directive beats a surrogate's new wish
lead: An advance directive that speaks to this decision outranks a surrogate who now wants something else.
lines: The document is interpreted for the decision in front of you, not as a slogan.
If the directive is silent, the surrogate uses substituted judgment.
When a patient lacks capacity, the surrogate decides by substituted judgment, then by best interest. A written directive that addresses the decision outranks a conflicting surrogate.
miss: Following the adult child in the room and ignoring the form the patient signed.
diagramAlt: Who decides. Written directive that fits this choice wins Else substituted judgment Else best interest

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 2.1.2, Decisions for Adult Patients Who Lack Capacity.
source.says: Assist the surrogate to make decisions in keeping with the standard of substituted judgment, basing decisions on: the patient’s preferences (if any) as expressed in an advance directive or as documented in the medical record.

title: Suspected elder abuse is reported
lead: Suspected elder abuse is reported through the required channel. The caregiver does not get to veto the report.
lines: Bruises in patterns, fear, and a dirty neglected patient are the clues.
Treat the injuries. The report is in addition, not instead.
Report on suspicion. You do not need proof, and the suspected abuser cannot veto the report.
Treat the injury and arrange a safe destination before discharge.
miss: Asking the suspected abuser for permission to report.
diagramAlt: Report abuse. Suspicion is enough. Proof is not Parent or caregiver cannot veto it Treat the injury and make the report

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 8.10, Preventing, Identifying and Treating Violence and Abuse.
source.says: Report suspected violence and abuse in keeping with applicable requirements.

title: A boundary is not a small gift that changes the prescription
lead: A gift, a date, or a social-media friendship that changes how you prescribe has crossed a professional boundary.
lines: Small tokens that do not change care are not the problem.
A romantic relationship with a current patient is not allowed.
The patient's dependence is the reason the rule exists.
A gift or a relationship that changes a prescription, especially a controlled substance, is a boundary violation.
miss: Accepting a vacation from a patient whose controlled substance you prescribe.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 1.2.8, Gifts from Patients.
source.says: Some patients may offer gifts or cash to secure or influence care or to secure preferential treatment. Not allow the gift or offer of a gift to influence the patient’s medical care.

title: Nonmaleficence stops the harm you were about to add
lead: Nonmaleficence means you do not add a treatment whose harm outweighs its benefit in this patient.
lines: A scan that cannot change the plan is a harm: contrast, radiation, cost, and a false positive.
Beneficence is the good you are trying to do. Both principles are in the same decision.
More treatment is not automatically more good.
miss: Ordering a test because it is available, when the result will not change what you do.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 5.5, Medically Ineffective Interventions.
source.says: Physicians should only recommend and provide interventions that are medically appropriate—i.e., scientifically grounded—and that reflect the physician’s considered medical judgment about the risks and likely benefits of available options in light of the patient’s goals for care.

title: Justice is the fair share, not the loudest request
lead: Justice means a scarce resource goes by a fair rule, not by who is in the room.
lines: The rule is stated. It is not invented after you see the patient's name.
A patient's wealth does not move them up a list that is supposed to be clinical.
The same rule applies when you like the patient.
A scarce bed or drug follows a clinical rule stated in advance. Friendship, fame, and anger do not move the list.
Apply the same rule on the next shift. Document the clinical reason.
miss: Moving a friend up the transplant or the scanner list.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 11.1.3, Allocating Limited Health Care Resources.
source.says: Base allocation policies on criteria relating to medical need, including urgency of need, likelihood and anticipated duration of benefit, and change in quality of life.

title: You do not abandon a patient you disagree with
lead: Discharging a patient from your care requires notice and a way to continue care. A disagreement is not abandonment.
lines: A capable refusal of one treatment does not end the relationship.
If you must end the relationship, you give time and alternatives.
Walking out of an ongoing emergency is abandonment.
miss: Telling a patient who refused one drug not to come back, with no handoff.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 1.1.5, Terminating a Patient-Physician Relationship.
source.says: Notify the patient (or authorized decision maker) long enough in advance to permit the patient to secure another physician. Facilitate transfer of care when appropriate.

title: Assent is what a child gives. Consent is what a parent gives
lead: A minor may assent. Legal consent for most care comes from a parent or guardian, except where the law lets the minor consent alone.
lines: Explain the plan in words the child can use.
An emergency in a child is treated when a parent cannot be reached.
Do not ask a child to sign a form the law says a parent must sign.
Assent is the child's agreement. Legal consent for most care is the parent's, except where statute lets the minor consent, often for sexual health, substance treatment, or emergency care.
miss: Taking a school-age child's signature as legal consent for elective surgery.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 2.2.1, Pediatric Decision Making.
source.says: The more mature a minor patient is, the better able to understand what a decision will mean, and the more clearly the child can communicate preferences, the stronger the ethical obligation to seek minor patients’ assent to treatment. In giving or withholding permission for medical treatment for their children, parents/guardians are expected to safeguard their children’s physical health and well-being.

title: A conflict of interest is named before the recommendation
lead: If you gain from the device or the drug you are recommending, you say so before the patient decides.
lines: The disclosure is specific. A vague mention is not enough.
The patient still gets the alternative that does not pay you.
Research consent is a separate form. A clinical consent does not enroll the patient in a study.
miss: Implanting a device you own a share of and mentioning it after the operation.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 11.2.2, Conflicts of Interest in Patient Care.
source.says: Under no circumstances may physicians place their own financial interests above the welfare of their patients.
